brief_summary:
This study examined whether an illustrated booklet could reduce anxiety in preschool children before magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performed under sedation. Fifty children aged 3 to 6 years were randomly assigned to receive either the usual spoken explanation or the same explanation plus an illustrated booklet called "MR Maceram" ("My MRI Adventure"). Families received the booklet at the anesthesia outpatient clinic before the scan day.

On the MRI day, children's anxiety was assessed in the waiting area and again in the preparation area before intravenous cannulation and sedative medication. Parents completed an anxiety questionnaire, and children's cooperation during intravenous cannulation was recorded. The main comparison was children's anxiety in the preparation area. The study was conducted at Kocaeli University Faculty of Medicine Hospital in Türkiye and is being registered after completion.
title: Visual Information Booklet and Anxiety in Preschool Children Undergoing Sedated MRI

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate whether acupuncture, specifically a combination of body acupuncture and ear vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS), can improve gastrointestinal function in critically ill elderly patients in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Gastrointestinal motility problems, such as delayed stomach emptying and constipation, are common in elderly ICU patients and can interfere with feeding, increase infection risk, and worsen outcomes. This research will test if adding acupuncture to standard care helps patients tolerate tube feeding (enteral nutrition) faster, reduces the need for intravenous nutrition, and improves overall recovery. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: standard care alone, standard care plus body acupuncture, or standard care plus both body acupuncture and ear vagus nerve stimulation. The study will compare the time it takes to achieve target feeding goals, changes in gastrointestinal function scores, and other clinical outcomes. This single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial will enroll 60 elderly patients from the Geriatric ICU of Jiangsu Province Hospital and aims to provide evidence for integrating traditional Chinese medicine into critical care practice.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University
primary_outcomes: Time to Achieve Enteral Nutrition Target
title: Ear-Vagus Nerve Stimulation and Body Acupuncture for Gut Motility in Elderly ICU Patients

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, non-interventional, observational study to evaluate the accuracy of 2 US (ultrasound) biomarkers that quantify liver tissue fat and stiffness: UDFF (ultrasound-derived fat fraction) and pSWE (point shear wave elastography) for determining MRI-defined eligibility for resmetirom (REZDIFFRA®) treatment and for monitoring treatment response using MRI-PDFF (proton density fat fraction) and MRE (magnetic resonance elastography) as reference standards.

Study Centers Planned:

3 clinical practice facilities in Houston TX .

Study Rationale:

MASLD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease ) is a growing global epidemic and the most common liver disease worldwide. Approximately 25% of adults in the United States alone have hepatic steatosis in the absence of significant alcohol consumption and 1 in 4 of these adults are presumed to have MASH.

MASH has a higher likelihood of progression to irreversible liver damage including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

Despite advancements in the field, there is still a high unmet need for technologies to accurately and reliably grade liver steatosis and stage liver fibrosis for applications related to patient identification and monitoring response to therapeutic intervention.

The association between hepatic steatosis and fibrosis progression underscores the need to have accurate and reliable noninvasive tools to aid in the assessment and monitoring of both liver steatosis and fibrosis.

The combination of 2 US (ultrasound) biomarkers that quantify liver tissue fat and stiffness (UDFF and pSWE) may aid clinicians in streamlining patient care pathways and potentially avoid unwanted and invasive medical intervention.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic performance of UDFF (ultrasound-derived fat fraction)
Diagnostic performance of Ultrasound pSWE (point shear wave elastography)
title: Ultrasound Biomarkers for Assessing Eligibility and Response to Resmetirom Therapy

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to learn if comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) and access to mobile sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services in secondary schools can improve short- and long-term health, well-being, social and economic outcomes among adolescents and young people in two districts of Sierra Leone. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. How do CSE and mobile SRH services (individually and combined) change adolescent SRHR, well-being and socioeconomic outcomes in the short term and in the longer term (over 3 years)?
2. What are the economic costs of providing CSE and mobile SRH services?
3. How cost-effective is the provision of CSE and mobile SRH services, given its potential impact on health, socioeconomic, and well-being outcomes?
4. To what extent are CSE and mobile SRH services being implemented according to the original plan and timeline?

Researchers will compare schools receiving CSE and mobile SRH services to schools not receiving these services, to see if adolescent SRHR, well-being and socioeconomic outcomes are better in those schools that received the services. The trial will compare four groups of schools, each with 60 participating schools:

1. No additional services (control schools)
2. Only CSE
3. Only mobile SRH services
4. CSE and mobile SRH services

The implementation of these services will be led by Marie Stopes Sierra Leone (MSSL) in collaboration with the Ministry of Education. MSSL will ensure that participating schools:

* Attend teacher training on the CSE curriculum before the study starts, followed by yearly refresher training during the study
* Have sufficient time allocated to CSE in the weekly school schedule
* Have adequate teaching materials \& equipment to teach CSE
* Have guidance counsellors in each school who will monitor the implementation of CSE
* Have a designated "safe space" which adolescents can access for menstrual products and care.
* Have access to mobile SRH services (provided by MSSL staff) on the school premises 3 times per school year
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYW) Using (or Whose Partner Uses) a Modern Contraceptive Method (mCPR)
Proportion of AGYW Whose Contraceptive Use or Non-Use Is Concordant with Their Fertility Preferences (Preference-Aligned Fertility Management)
Proportion of AGYW with Decision-Making Autonomy over Family Planning
Proportion of AGYW and Adolescent Boys and Young Men (ABYM) Who Have Dropped Out of School

brief_summary: This study compared the effects of two resistance training periodization models, block periodization and daily undulating periodization, on muscular strength and force production in healthy young adults with limited resistance training experience. Participants were randomly assigned to a block periodization group, a daily undulating periodization group, or a non-training control group. The two training groups completed three supervised resistance training sessions per week for 12 weeks. Both training programs used the same exercises and were designed to have similar total training volume and average programmed relative intensity, but differed in how training volume and intensity were organized over time. Muscular strength and force production were assessed before and after the intervention using the isometric mid-thigh pull and single-joint isometric strength testing of the knee and elbow.

This is a phase III clinical trial with a multicenter, randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled design to evaluate the protective efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of the recombinant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine (CHO cell) in individuals aged 60 and above.

Sample Size and Trial Grouping: This trial plans to enroll 25,000 trial participants aged ≥60 years (with approximately 30% aged 70 and above), with a relatively balanced gender distribution. Participants of each age group (60-69 years old, ≥70 years old) will be randomly assigned to the trial group and the placebo group in a 1:1 ratio. The sample size for the immunogenicity subgroup is not calculated based on statistical power. Referring to similar clinical trials of RSV vaccines and in conjunction with the immunogenicity observation objectives of this trial, the first 300 trial participants (including those from both age groups) from each site under the leading institution will be included in the immunogenicity subgroup, for a total of 1,200 participants.

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect of the cold needle technique on pain and patient satisfaction during intramuscular injections administered to the ventrogluteal site.

The study was conducted in the internal medicine clinics of Prof. Dr. Cemil Taşçıoğlu City Hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye. A total of 78 adult patients receiving intramuscular vitamin B12 injections as part of their prescribed treatment participated in the study.

Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=40) or a control group (n=38). The intervention group received intramuscular injections using a cooled needle, while the control group received injections using the standard technique. Only the injection needle was cooled; the medication was not cooled.

Pain intensity and patient satisfaction were assessed after the injection using Visual Analog Scales (VAS).

The study aims to determine whether the cold needle technique reduces injection-related pain and improves patient satisfaction compared with the standard intramuscular injection technique.
title: The Effect of the Cold Needle Technique on Pain and Patient Satisfaction Levels During Intramuscular Injection Administered to the Ventrogluteal Site

brief_summary:
ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, and timely reperfusion with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) is the gold-standard treatment1. Current guidelines recommend a door-to-balloon (DTB) time of 90 minutes or less, as the benefits of PPCI increase in direct correlation with the brevity of reperfusion time.

However, there is consistent epidemiological evidence that STEMI patients presenting during off-hours (nights, weekends, and holidays) experience delays in reperfusion and worse in-hospital outcomes compared to those presenting during regular business hours. Two competing hypotheses dominate the literature. The systems hypothesis suggests that delays in care delivery during nights and weekends-including longer catheterization laboratory activation time, reduced availability of experienced operators, and logistical constraints-are the primary drivers of worse outcomes. In support of this, some studies have found that the mortality difference between off-hours and on-hours presentations is attenuated after adjusting for DTB time (Chung et al., 2020), suggesting that system-level process measures may be actionable targets for quality improvement.

Alternatively, the intrinsic severity hypothesis suggests that nocturnal STEMI presentations represent inherently more severe infarcts-characterized by higher thrombus burden, larger myocardial infarction size, and more frequent complications such as cardiogenic shock-independent of how rapidly reperfusion is achieved. Recent studies examining circadian variation in infarct size and myocardial injury biomarkers have found evidence of larger infarcts and worse systolic function in nocturnal-onset STEMI, with long-term mortality implications.

Critically, the vast majority of evidence in this field derives from retrospective registry data, particularly from North American and Western European cohorts. Data from the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, where demographic and healthcare system profiles differ substantially from developed nations, are essentially absent from the literature. Furthermore, contemporary data on the prospective relationships between time-of-PPCI, operator experience, procedural quality parameters (such as myocardial blush grade and ST-segment resolution), and outcomes remain limited.

A prospective study with granular intra-procedural data collection offers the opportunity to: (1) quantify the magnitude of the off-hours effect in a Middle Eastern context; (2) decompose the DTB time into its components to identify specific system bottlenecks; (3) assess whether operator seniority and team composition confound or mediate the off-hours effect6; and (4) evaluate whether procedural quality metrics (reperfusion grade, thrombus burden, microvascular perfusion) differ between daytime and nighttime PPCI and contribute to outcome disparities independent of system factors.
title: On vs Off-hour PPCI in STEMI Patients

brief_summary: LONGEVITY-NEXT is a single-center, non-profit observational study designed to assess early non-invasive determinants of cardiometabolic, functional, behavioral, and environmental health in children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 years from the general population. Participants will undergo a standardized 15-20-minute non-invasive assessment including anthropometric measurements, blood pressure and heart rate, handgrip strength, dietary habits and adherence to the Mediterranean diet, physical activity, recreational screen time, sleep duration, tobacco smoke exposure, early-life factors, chronic health conditions, and family cardiometabolic history. The primary outcome is the distribution of the number of unfavorable cardiometabolic, behavioral, and environmental health domains per participant. The study involves no experimental treatment, drug, investigational medical device, invasive procedure, or modification of usual care. Optional repeated assessments may occur opportunistically during the study while participants remain between 6 and 17 years of age.

brief_summary: This phase I trial tests the safety and feasibility of giving pasritamig before surgery in patients with unfavorable intermediate-risk, high-risk, or very high-risk localized prostate cancer. Pasritamig is a bispecific antibody that works by bringing immune cells called T cells close to prostate cancer cells that express KLK2, which may help the immune system attack the cancer. Giving pasritamig before radical prostatectomy may help researchers determine how the drug affects prostate cancer and the immune cells within the tumor.
primary_outcomes: Change in intratumoral CD3+ T-cell density
title: Testing Pasritamig Before Surgery for the Treatment of Localized Prostate Cancer

title: Combination of Rituximab and Cyclosporine in the Treatment of Primary Membranous Nephropathy

brief_summary:
Rotator cuff-related shoulder pain (RCRSP) is one of the most common musculoskeletal disorders presenting in primary care. It is frequently associated with persistent pain, disability, healthcare utilisation and work absenteeism. Exercise-based physiotherapy is recommended as first-line management in clinical practice guidelines, yet its average effects on pain and disability are modest and a substantial proportion of people remain symptomatic several months after onset. Patient education is also recommended, and trials conducted in people with persistent symptoms suggest that education-based care may produce improvements comparable to those obtained with progressive exercise. However, the effectiveness of a structured educational intervention as a first-line management strategy during the acute phase of RCRSP remains unclear.

SHOULD Education lead Rehabilitation? (SHOULD-ER) is a multicentre, pragmatic, parallel-group, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial comparing a personalised, multimodal educational intervention with usual physiotherapy care in adults presenting with acute non-traumatic RCRSP of less than six weeks duration. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the trial arms for a 12-week treatment period, with follow-up to 24 weeks.

The primary objective is to determine whether the educational intervention is non-inferior to usual physiotherapy care regarding improvement in shoulder pain and disability at 12 weeks, measured by the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI). Secondary outcomes include pain-related function, self-efficacy, fear-avoidance beliefs, quality of life, sleep quality, patient satisfaction and healthcare costs.

A nested qualitative study and a within-trial economic evaluation are embedded in the trial. An exploratory analysis of prognostic factors will also be conducted with a secondary analysis.
primary_outcomes: Change in Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI) total Score
title: Personalised Education Versus Usual Physiotherapy for Acute Rotator Cuff-Related Shoulder Pain

brief_summary: This study evaluated the effects of IHSAN Model-based Islamic spiritual care compared with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)-based psychological support and routine care in Muslim patients with cancer receiving radiotherapy. A total of 137 patients were initially recruited, and 17 were subsequently excluded because they did not continue participation or did not complete the required study questionnaires. The remaining 120 participants were allocated by drawing lots to three groups: Spiritual Support, Psychological Support, or Control, with 40 participants in each group. Anxiety, depressive symptoms, psychological distress, and spirituality were assessed before and after the intervention. The study examined whether changes in these outcomes differed among the three groups.
lead_sponsor: Dr Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Ankara Oncology Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale - Anxiety Subscale (HADS-A) Score
Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale - Depression Subscale (HADS-D) Score
title: Islamic Spiritual Care Versus Psychological Support in Radiotherapy

brief_summary:
Peripheral arterial disease can reduce blood flow to the legs. This study will examine how blood flow patterns in the leg arteries differ between people with peripheral arterial disease and people without the disease.

Researchers will use existing computed tomography angiography (CTA) images and medical records from participants who previously received CTA as part of routine clinical care. Three-dimensional models of the leg arteries will be created from these images. Computer simulations will then be used to study how changes in blood flow entering the arteries and resistance in smaller downstream blood vessels affect blood flow patterns. The researchers will compare these responses between participants with and without peripheral arterial disease.

This study uses only existing medical records and images. No new participants will be recruited, and no additional examinations or treatments will be performed for research purposes. The goal is to better understand blood flow characteristics associated with peripheral arterial disease.
title: Hemodynamic Characteristics of Peripheral Arterial Disease Using Computational Fluid Dynamics

brief_summary:
Scar tissue can form around a repaired tendon and restrict finger movement. This study will evaluate whether repeated ultrasound-guided normal saline injections, in addition to standard postoperative rehabilitation, can help prevent and treat tendon adhesion after surgical repair of zone II flexor tendon injuries.

The study is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial involving 80 adults aged 18 to 60 years with a zone II flexor tendon rupture in the index, middle, ring, or little finger. Participants will be assigned to one of two groups, with 40 participants in each group. Participants in both groups will receive the same standard postoperative rehabilitation treatment, including early active finger mobilization. In addition to this rehabilitation, the experimental group will receive ultrasound-guided percutaneous injections of 1 mL of normal saline at the tendon adhesion site on postoperative days 7, 14, and 21. The control group will receive standard postoperative rehabilitation alone, without postoperative normal saline injections.

The primary outcome is total active motion of the repaired finger at 3 months after surgery. Finger movement, pain, hand function, postoperative finger infection, and tendon rupture will also be assessed at the scheduled follow-up visits.
primary_outcomes: Total Active Motion at 3 Months After Surgery
title: Ultrasound-Guided Repeated Saline Injections to Prevent and Treat Tendon Adhesions After Hand Tendon Repair

brief_summary:
The goal of this cross-sectional observational study is to examine the relationship between swimming stroke specialization and scapular movement and shoulder function in healthy competitive swimmers aged 13 to 19 years. The study will include 80 swimmers: 20 specializing in each of four strokes-freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly. Each stroke group will include 10 males and 10 females. Eligible swimmers will have at least 5 years of competitive swimming experience and at least 1 year of continuous participation in sanctioned competitions. Swimmers with a major upper-limb injury or surgery in the previous 6 months will not be included. The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Is swimming stroke specialization related to scapular dyskinesia, assessed by measuring scapular upward rotation?
* Is swimming stroke specialization related to the strength of the serratus anterior, middle trapezius, and lower trapezius muscles?
* Is swimming stroke specialization related to shoulder internal rotation range of motion, posterior shoulder capsular tightness, and pectoralis minor length?

Researchers will compare the measurements among the four stroke-specialization groups to determine whether scapular movement and shoulder function differ by stroke type. Assessments will be performed on the participants' dominant side.

Participants will:

* Complete a Google Form providing demographic and swimming-related information, including age, sex, height, weight, body mass index, dominant side, breathing side, and stroke specialization
* Have scapular upward rotation assessed from photographs taken at rest and at 90- and 120-degree arm elevation positions; the photographs will be analyzed using Kinovea software
* Have serratus anterior, middle trapezius, and lower trapezius muscle strength measured using a handheld dynamometer
* Have shoulder internal rotation range of motion measured using a bubble inclinometer
* Complete physical assessments of posterior shoulder capsular tightness and pectoralis minor length

This is an observational study. Participants will go through treatment or medication will be given.
primary_outcomes: Scapular Dyskinesis through scapular upward rotation angle by 2D motion analysis.
title: Relation Between Swimming Stroke Types And Scapular Dyskinesia In Swimmers: A Cross - Sectional Study

brief_summary:
This study is designed to evaluate the clinical performance of the UllCORE BSI Test, an investigational molecular diagnostic test intended to detect microorganisms and selected antimicrobial resistance markers directly from whole blood in patients with suspected bloodstream infection or sepsis.

Participants enrolled in the study will have blood collected at the same time as blood samples obtained for standard-of-care blood culture testing. Study blood samples will be tested using the UllCORE BSI Test either as fresh samples or after frozen storage, according to the study protocol.

The results of the UllCORE BSI Test will be compared with standard-of-care microbiology results and, when applicable, additional testing methods to assess the diagnostic performance of the investigational test.

The UllCORE BSI Test results will not be used to guide patient care and will not be provided to treating healthcare professionals for clinical decision-making. Participation in the study will therefore not change the standard medical care received by participants.
primary_outcomes: Clinical Performance of the UllCORE ID BSI Test Assessed by Positive Percent Agreement (PPA) and Negative Percent Agreement (NPA)
title: Evaluation of Diagnostic Accuracy and Clinical Performance of the UIICORE BSI Test

brief_summary: Conventional clinical evaluation of dental occlusion relies predominantly on qualitative indicators such as articulating papers, metallic foils, and silicone-based materials and the accuracy of these indicators may be influenced by material thickness, moisture contamination, and subjective interpretation. Quantitative assessment of occlusal contacts in direct and indirect posterior restorations may help clinicians to establish and maintain harmonious and proper dental occlusion. To assess the level of static and dynamic occlusal contact surfaces in direct and indirect restorations, clinically and quantitatively. Also, to compare outcomes between clinicians with two different levels of clinical experience, immediately and one month after the restorative procedures. Patients requiring restoration for maxillary or mandibular first molars were treated either with direct nanohybrid resin composite (Neo Spectra ST HV A2, Dentsply) restorations or indirect CAD/CAM (Cerasmart 270 HT A2, GC) restorations. The direct (n =30) and indirect (n =30) restorations of postgraduate clinicians and direct restorations (n=30) of undergraduate clinicians (5th grade) were compared immediately (T1) and one month (T2) after the restorative procedures. A single dental technician performed the digital design and the milling of all indirect restorations. Static and dynamic occlusal contact surfaces of the teeth were quantitatively assessed through the collected digital scans by an intraoral scanner (iTero Element 5D, Align), using a computer software program (ChairsideCAD 3.1, Exocad, Align), by setting contact distances to 10, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, and 350 μm, gradually. The static contacts were assessed by calculating the percentage of the occlusal contact surfaces to the entire occlusal contact surface for each restored tooth, using the ImageJ software program (National Institutes of Health). The dynamic contacts were assessed according to the presence (positive) or absence (negative), regarding 4 lateral movements of the mandibular arch (0.5, 1, 2, and 3 mm on the working side) using a virtual articulator integrated to the ChairsideCAD.
primary_outcomes: The level of static and dynamic occlusal contacts of direct and indirect restorations
title: Clinical Assessment of Dynamic and Static Occlusal Contacts in Direct and Indirect Posterior Restorations

brief_summary: Congenital hearing loss is one of the most common sensory disorders of childhood, and the structural, immunologic and oxidative mechanisms involved in its development are incompletely understood. This case-control study aims to evaluate serum alpha-tectorin and interleukin-10 (IL-10) levels and thiol-disulfide homeostasis in children with congenital sensorineural hearing loss (cochlear implant users and hearing aid users) compared with healthy children with normal hearing. The findings are expected to contribute to a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying congenital hearing loss and to the identification of potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers.
title: Alpha-Tectorin, Interleukin-10 and Thiol-Disulfide Homeostasis in Children With Congenital Hearing Loss

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to compare the pain-relieving effects of two different nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), intravenous ibuprofen and intravenous dexketoprofen, in adults who present to the emergency department with isolated rib fractures. Patients with rib fractures confirmed by a computed tomography (CT) scan and experiencing moderate to severe pain will randomly receive either 800 mg of intravenous ibuprofen or 50 mg of intravenous dexketoprofen. The researchers will measure pain levels using a 100-mm Visual Analog Scale (VAS) before the treatment and at 30, 60, and 120 minutes after receiving the medication to evaluate which drug provides better pain relief. The study will also track how many patients require additional rescue pain medication and record any side effects that occur during the observation period.
primary_outcomes: Absolute pain reduction from baseline to 60 minutes (ΔVAS0-60)
title: Ibuprofen Versus Dexketoprofen in Rib Fractures

brief_summary:
Osteopathy is recognized as a beneficial complementary approach for cancer patients. By addressing tissue mobility, circulation, and muscle tension, it helps improve physical comfort, reduce musculoskeletal pain, and foster better functional recovery. Several studies have shown that osteopathy can help reduce pain intensity and improve the quality of life for patients undergoing cancer treatment.

Combining hypnosis with osteopathy could thus optimize treatment outcomes by integrating a holistic approach that addresses both physical and psychological needs. The aim of this study is to evaluate the impact of combined osteopathy and hypnosis treatment compared to osteopathic treatment alone in cancer patients, particularly regarding pain with a strong emotional component.
title: Impact of Therapeutic Osteopathy-hypnosis on Cancer Patients.

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to investigate the association between subcutaneous fat index, paraspinal muscle characteristics, facet morphology, and lumbar facet joint degeneration in adults with chronic low back pain. The study will use lumbar magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) obtained as part of routine clinical care. The study will evaluate whether subcutaneous fat index is associated with moderate-to-severe lumbar facet joint degeneration and will also examine the relationships of disc degeneration, facet morphology, paraspinal muscle characteristics, and pain severity with facet joint degeneration.
primary_outcomes: Association between subcutaneous fat index and moderate-to-severe lumbar facet joint degeneration
title: Association of Subcutaneous Fat Index, Paraspinal Muscle Characteristics, and Facet Morphology With Lumbar Facet Joint Degeneration

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate whether listening to the recitation of Surah Ar-Rahman (Murottal) before bedtime can help improve anxiety and sleep quality in hospitalized children with blood cancer. Twenty children aged 8-12 years will be divided into two groups: one group will receive standard care plus the Murottal intervention for 7 days, while the other group will receive standard care only. Anxiety and sleep quality will be measured using validated questionnaires (SCARED and SDSC) before and after the intervention. We hope this study will provide evidence that Murottal can be a safe, non-invasive, and culturally appropriate supportive therapy for pediatric cancer patients.
primary_outcomes: Change in Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders (SCARED) Score
Change in Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC) Score
title: Murottal as Adjunctive Intervention in Pediatric

brief_summary: Glaucoma is a chronic, progressive neuro-ophthalmic condition that leads to irreversible loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide. It is associated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), but many patients continue to experience vision loss even with controlled IOP. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a key mechanism in RGC damage, leading to interest in neuroprotective treatments. Various compounds like citicoline (CIT), homotaurine (HOMO), vitamin B3 (nicotinamide), and pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) have shown potential in protecting RGCs, improving mitochondrial function, and reducing oxidative stress. This study aims to compare the effects of a combination supplement (NEUPROZIN MITO) containing CIT, HOMO, NAM, and PQQ with CIT alone (OPTIGEN) on contrast sensitivity, quality of life, and reading speed in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and controlled IOP. The study is a randomized, cross-over trial with two treatment groups, and outcomes will include changes in visual function, quality of life, and reading performance over 8 months. The sample size calculation suggests enrolling 44 patients to detect a clinically significant difference. This research will assess the effectiveness of mitochondrial-targeted therapies for glaucoma patients with controlled IOP.
interventions: citicoline 500 mg + nicotinamide 54 mg + PQQ 5 mg + Homotaurine 50 mg fixed combination tablet (Neuprozin mito)
lead_sponsor: Università degli Studi 'G. d'Annunzio' Chieti e Pescara
primary_outcomes: Unravelling the effects of Nicotinamide/Pyrroloquinolone Quinone /Citicoline/Homotaurine fixed combination on reading performance in glaucoma
Unravelling the effects of Nicotinamide/Pyrroloquinolone Quinone /Citicoline/Homotaurine fixed combination on contrast sensitivity,
1. Unravelling the effects of Nicotinamide/Pyrroloquinolone Quinone /Citicoline/Homotaurine fixed combination on quality of life.
title: Unravelling the Effects of Nicotinamide/Pyrroloquinolone Quinone /Citicoline/Homotaurine Fixed Combination on Contrast Sensitivity, Quality of Life, and Reading Performance in Glaucoma

brief_summary: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) may frequently recur even after successful canalith repositioning maneuvers (CRMs). This study investigates whether the addition of vitamin K₂ to vitamin D₃ offers additional benefits for reducing recurrence. It involved 404 adults treated at a single otolaryngology center in Amman, Jordan, divided into three groups: combined D3K2 (n = 212), D3 alone (n = 105), and CRM alone (n = 87). The study used modified Poisson regression to analyze 12-month recurrence rates, adjusting for confounding factors. Recurrence was clinically confirmed during the follow-up period.
interventions: Combined vitamin D₃ and K₂ supplementation
title: BPPV Recurrence After CRM With & Without Supplementation

title: Multicenter Prospective Observational Study on Prostate Salvage Using High-dose-rate Brachytherapy.

brief_summary: This study evaluates the long-term safety and tolerability of linerixibat in Japanese adults with cholestatic pruritus in primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) who previously participated in the linerixibat long-term safety and efficacy study, LLSAT (NCT04167358). Participants will continue receiving linerixibat while researchers monitor adverse events and other safety measures to better understand the long-term safety of treatment and provide continued access to therapy.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious AEs (SAEs)
Number of Participants With AEs by Severity

title: Early Outcomes of Thoracoscopic Anatomical Lesion Resection for Congenital Lung Malformations in Children: A Single-Center Experience in a Limited-Resource Country

brief_summary: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease of the sinonasal mucosa whose metabolic and immunologic mechanisms are incompletely understood. This prospective case-control study aims to characterize metabolic and immunologic biomarkers in patients with CRSwNP compared with control subjects. Nasal tissue and peripheral blood samples will be analyzed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for free amino acid and carnitine/acylcarnitine profiles, and levels of interleukin-40 (IL-40), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) will be measured by ELISA. The findings are expected to contribute to understanding disease pathogenesis and to identifying potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
primary_outcomes: Tissue and serum free amino acid and carnitine/acylcarnitine profiles
Interleukin-40 (IL-40) levels in tissue and serum
title: Metabolic and Immunologic Biomarkers in Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps

brief_summary: This observational study uses existing U.S. specialty oncology electronic health records to emulate the SUNLIGHT trial. It compares survival among adults with metastatic colorectal cancer who began trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab or trifluridine-tipiracil alone after prior systemic treatment. Treatment was chosen during routine care; the study did not assign treatment. The main outcome is time to death from any cause. Investigators will compare the real-world estimate with the published estimate from the randomized SUNLIGHT trial.
title: Emulation of the SUNLIGHT Trial Using Specialty Oncology Electronic Health Records Databases

brief_summary:
This study tested whether a home-based exercise program helps older adults with Parkinson's disease keep the improvements they gain from a community balance program.

Participants lived in small towns and rural communities in Oklahoma, where access to movement disorder specialists is limited. All participants first took part in a three-month community-based recreational therapy balance program. At the end of those three months, participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group continued with a home-based program for twelve weeks, which included an exercise manual, instructional videos, and a weekly telephone call from a researcher. The other group received general wellness guidance without follow-up contact.

Participants were assessed three times: before the community program began, at three months, and at six months. The assessments measured walking speed, stride length, and cadence; postural stability; concern about falling; anxiety and depression; social connectedness; and quality of life.

The purpose of the study was to learn whether continued support at home helps people hold onto the gains they make in a community program, and how quickly those gains are lost without that support.
interventions: Home-based exercise program with remote checking and coaching
title: Home-Based Exercise Program After Community Balance Training for Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate \[68Ga\]FAPI-46 whole-body PET/MRI as a diagnostic tool to improve tumour lesion examination at primary staging, during treatment control and at relapse in paediatric sarcoma patients.

The main questions the trial aim to answer are:

* Is \[68Ga\]FAPI-46 whole-body PET/MRI better at detecting malignancy in paediatric sarcoma patients compared to current standard of care imaging modalities?
* Is the overall diagnostic performance of \[68Ga\]FAPI-46 whole-body PET/MRI feasible to implement in clinical practice?

The intervention of \[68Ga\]FAPI-46 will be compared to current standard of care imaging modalities. All participants will receive their standard of care imaging protocol as rutinely scheduled, which includes:

* A localized MRI scan of the tumour region and
* An \[18F\]FDG whole-body PET/CT scan

In addition to the standard of care imaging protocol, all patients will receive the following experimental scans:

* An \[18F\]FDG whole-body PET/MRI
* A \[68Ga\]FAPI-46 whole-body PET/MRI
* A \[68Ga\]FAPI-46 whole-body PET/CT

All patients and legal guardians will fill out questionnaires on their experiences. Patients may undergo the entire trial imaging procedures, including the standard of care imaging protocol and the experimental scans, a maximum of five times.
title: Paediatric Sarcoma, Hybrid Imaging & FAPI - Raising the Diagnostic Standard for Paediatric Sarcoma Patients, Combining Novel Radiotracer FAPI and Whole-body PET/MRI

brief_summary: This trial is a phase II, randomized, open label study designed to evaluate safety, tolerability and efficacy of CC-1, a bispecific antibody (bsAb) with PSMAxCD3 specificity, and of VACXS15-PC01, a prostate cancer (PC)-specific multi-peptide vaccine, both administered as single agent or in combination to patients affected with biochemical recurrence (BCR) of PC after local therapy with curative intent. Patients will not receive other treatments during trial participation.
primary_outcomes: PSA response defined as ≥50% reduction in PSA at FU1 compared to baseline.
title: Multi-peptide Vaccination and Bispecific PSMAxCD3 Antibody Treatment in Patients With Prostate Cancer

brief_summary: This first-in-human, open-label, multicenter study evaluates K-1728 administered as monotherapy and in combination in participants with advanced or metastatic solid tumors. The study assesses the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary antitumor activity of K-1728.
primary_outcomes: Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD)/Maximum Efficacious Dose (MED) and Recommended Phase 2 Dose (RP2D)
Incidence of Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
title: A Phase 1/2a Study of K-1728 in Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
Menopause is a biological process characterized by the permanent cessation of menstruation, often accompanied by vasomotor symptoms, sleep disturbances, anxiety, and impaired quality of life. In primary healthcare settings, structured lifestyle interventions offer low-cost, safe, and sustainable non-pharmacological management strategies.

The objective of this prospective, randomized controlled trial is to evaluate whether a structured lifestyle educational intervention leads to significant improvements in menopausal symptom severity, sleep quality, and anxiety levels compared with a control group receiving routine clinical care among perimenopausal and postmenopausal women aged 40 to 55 years. Primary and secondary outcomes are evaluated using the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) at baseline and at 24 weeks.
lead_sponsor: Konya Beyhekim Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) Total Score at 24 Weeks
title: Effect of Lifestyle Intervention on Menopausal Symptoms, Sleep Quality, and Anxiety in Peri- and Postmenopausal Women

brief_summary:
The ENRICH Study is a single-arm, single-site, mixed-methods feasibility and pilot implementation study examining a culturally adapted, nurse-led model of care for social frailty among community-dwelling older adults in one primary health center in Manila City, Philippines.

The study comprises four sequential phases: (1) Filipino translation and cultural adaptation of the Montayre Social Frailty-10 (MSF-10); (2) participatory co-design and refinement of the Social Frailty Care Bundle (SFCB); (3) nurse training and competency assessment; and (4) a three-month pilot implementation. It will assess feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, workflow fit, recruitment, retention, follow-up completion, and implementation readiness to inform a future definitive trial.
interventions: Group activities (i.e., low impact exercise), peer counseling, volunteering
primary_outcomes: Consent rate among eligible older adults
Fidelity of Social Frailty Care Bundle (SFCB) delivery
title: ENRICH Study: A Mixed-methods Feasibility Study of a Nurse-led Model of Care for Social Frailty in Philippine Primary Care

brief_summary: This study will translate and culturally adapt the Patients' Endorsement of a Biopsychosocial Model of Chronic Pain Scale (PEB) into Turkish and evaluate how well and consistently it measures the views of adults with chronic pain. The study will take place at the Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation outpatient clinic of Bilecik Training and Research Hospital. At least 200 adults will be included in the main sample. Participants will complete questionnaires that are expected to take 10 to 15 minutes. An additional 20 people who will not be included in the main sample will take part in a pilot assessment. Fifty participants from the main sample will complete the PEB Scale again after two weeks. No treatment or intervention will be assigned.
primary_outcomes: Construct validity and internal consistency of the Turkish PEB Scale
title: Turkish Version of a Scale Measuring How People View Chronic Pain

title: Efficacy of Intensive Visual Simulation (IVS) Before Exoskeleton-assisted Step Training in Patients With Hemisensory Syndrome With Brain Injury of Vascular Etiology.

brief_summary: Episodic memory allows us to project ourselves back in time to mentally re-experience the past in vivid detail. This remarkable feat helps to define our personal identities and enables context-appropriate predictions that guide adaptive behavior. Unfortunately, episodic memory loss is a common cognitive consequence of neurological disease, psychiatric disorders, and normative aging, that reflects dysfunction in the hippocampus and the neocortical network to which it connects. This decline can present along a range of severity that spans an impoverished ability to recollect fine-grained event details, e.g., the color of the shirt your spouse was wearing at a birthday party, to forgetting course-grained event details, e.g., having attended a birthday party last weekend. Treating these kinds of memory loss remains challenging because interventions must target information that is definitionally idiosyncratic. However, recent methodological and theoretical advances in cognitive neuroscience reveal novel strategies that may solve this problem. Evidence from behavioral, neuroimaging, and computational modeling studies suggest that the degree to which episodic memories overlap in the hippocampus can be modified in a predictable, experience-dependent manner. Specifically, strong concurrent reactivation of multiple memories can enhance recall of coarse-grained episodic information by increasing hippocampal integration. Conversely, coupling strong and moderate reactivation of memories can enhance recall of fine-grained episodic information be increasing hippocampal differentiation. Consistent with this idea, recent evidence suggests that using a smartphone to record and subsequently replay real-world memory cues can indeed improve episodic memory by reducing representational overlap among memories in the hippocampus. Against this background, this proposal is organized around two primary aims. First, we seek to establish smartphone-guided memory reactivation protocols that selectively promote integration and differentiation of real-world episodic memories in the hippocampus. Experiments in this aim will specifically ask whether unstructured and structured (in terms of narrative, space, and time) reactivation can be used to achieve these outcomes. Second, we will ask whether the benefits of memory reactivation are associated with behavioral and representational costs. Experiments in this aim will probe for undesirable downsides that accompany, or potentially explain, reactivation-based improvements in episodic memory. Our approach combines smartphone technology, pattern-based analysis of functional neuroimaging data, and careful characterization of recall data with neurocognitive theory inspired by computational models of learning mechanisms. Achieving our aims will establish an empirical foundation on which future interventions can be built to systematically target real-world episodic memories at a level of abstraction, i.e., fine-grained vs. coarse-grained detail, that is appropriate for the severity of memory loss.
interventions: Participants use a smartphone to replay self-generated autobiographical memory cues.
title: fMRI Studies of Memory and Perception

brief_summary: This implementation study evaluates an integrated digital e-clinic designed to provide mental health, psychosocial, and reproductive health support to women and adolescent girls in Jordan, including Jordanian and Syrian refugee participants and other vulnerable groups. The e-clinic provides individualized psychosocial support, evidence-based educational content, self-help resources, scheduled interactions with trained healthcare providers, and referral pathways for participants requiring additional or specialized services. Participants complete baseline assessments before using the e-clinic and follow-up assessments approximately three months after baseline or following completion of the intervention. The study evaluates changes in mental health and well-being outcomes as well as acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, accessibility, digital health literacy, reproductive health knowledge and attitudes, service utilization, participant satisfaction, privacy, and engagement with the e-clinic.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the similarity of pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters following a single intravenous infusion of QL1209 (Perjeta® biosimilar candidate) and Perjeta® (Pertuzumab) in healthy male participants.

Participants will receive a single intravenous infusion of QL1209 or US-Perjeta® 420 mg on D1, followed by observation until Day 99 postdose for PK, safety and immunogenicity assessments.
title: Comparative Study of QL1209 and Perjeta® in Healthy Male Participants

brief_summary:
Passive leg raising (PLR) transiently increases venous return and cardiac preload and is commonly used to predict fluid responsiveness in critically ill patients. Repeated fluid boluses contribute to fluid overload in septic shock, whereas PLR may provide similar hemodynamic effects without fluid administration.

Before evaluating repeated PLR in septic shock patients, it is necessary to determine whether the cardiac output response to PLR remains present during repeated PLR maneuvers.

SYSLE-1 is a prospective interventional physiological crossover study conducted in healthy volunteers. Participants will undergo six consecutive passive leg raising sessions performed either during spontaneous breathing or non-invasive ventilation, in randomized order. The study aims to determine whether the increase in cardiac output induced by the first PLR maneuver persists during repeated PLR sessions.
primary_outcomes: Change in cardiac output during the sixth passive leg raising session compared with the first passive leg raising session, for each day of study procedure
title: Effect of Systematic and Sequential Leg Elevation on Cardiac Output in Healthy Volunteers

brief_summary: This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness of using a patient's own subepithelial connective tissue graft as a natural barrier membrane during simultaneous hard and soft tissue augmentation in areas of the jawbone with insufficient horizontal width. The procedure will be performed during delayed dental implant placement. The study aims to assess changes in hard and soft tissue dimensions and the clinical outcomes of this approach in patients with horizontally deficient alveolar ridges.
conditions: Hard and Soft Tissue Augmentation During Delayed Implant Placement
interventions: Subepithelial Connective Tissue Graft as an Autogenous Barrier Membrane for Hard and Soft Tissue Augmentation in Horizontally Deficient Ridges during delayed implant placement
title: Effectiveness of Subepithelial Connective Tissue Graft as an Autogenous Barrier Membrane for Hard and Soft Tissue Augmentation in Horizontally Deficient Ridges During Delayed Implant Placement

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot interventional study (pre-post design) is to learn if a co-designed wrist-hand orthosis can improve acceptability compared to a conventional orthosis in children aged 6 to 14 years with neuromotor disorders following acquired or congenital brain injury.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does a wrist-hand orthosis developed through a co-design process with the pediatric patient show greater acceptability - measured via the Technological Acceptance Measure (TAM-3) - compared to the conventional orthosis already used by the patient? Does the co-designed orthosis guarantee at least equivalent functional performance to the conventional orthosis, as assessed through upper limb kinematic analysis?

Researchers will compare the co-designed orthosis to the conventional orthosis to see if the co-design and personalization process improves acceptance, satisfaction, and functional outcomes.

Participants will:

Complete acceptance and satisfaction questionnaires (TAM-3 and QUEST 2.1) and undergo functional upper limb assessment while wearing their conventional orthosis Participate in two structured co-design workshops (\~1.5 hours each) involving creative and expressive activities to define preferences for their personalized orthosis Receive and wear the co-designed 3D-printed orthosis, then repeat functional assessments and questionnaires, and take part in a semi-structured interview about their co-design experience.
primary_outcomes: Change in wrist-hand orthosis acceptability as measured by the Technological Acceptance Measure (TAM-3) score between first and last study visit
title: Acceptability of Paediatric Wrist Orthoses Through Co-design

brief_summary:
Aerobic gymnastics requires repeated explosive movements, upper-body support elements, and the ability to maintain performance under fatigue. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluates the effects of Rhodiola rosea supplementation, acute caffeine ingestion, and their combination on sport-specific performance and recovery in female competitive aerobic gymnasts.

Ninety-six female aerobic gymnasts will be randomly assigned to placebo, Rhodiola rosea, caffeine, or combined Rhodiola rosea plus caffeine groups. All participants will complete an 8-week standardized aerobic gymnastics training program. Rhodiola rosea will be supplemented daily during the intervention period, while caffeine or matched placebo will be administered before post-intervention performance testing.

The primary outcome is the change in Specific Aerobic Gymnastics Anaerobic Test (SAGAT) total completion time. Secondary outcomes include neuromuscular performance, fatigue-related responses, perceived exertion, muscle soreness, and perceived recovery status.
primary_outcomes: Specific Aerobic Gymnastics Anaerobic Test (SAGAT) Total Completion Time
title: Combined Rhodiola Rosea and Caffeine Supplementation for Aerobic Gymnastics Performance

brief_summary:
The overall aims of this project are to undertake a women's health screening clinic on oral health and systemic health, linking the oral microbiome to hormonal status (menopause);

The follow quantitative and qualitative markers of oral health will be used:

* Salivary and systemic female hormone status
* Systemic/cardiovascular health markers, such as blood pressure, cholesterol and blood glucose
* Clinical oral health variables (markers of plaque and gum disease)
* Physiological and biochemical markers, such as salivary nitrate and nitrite
* Oral microbiome
* Breath analysis (volatile sulphur comounds)
* Perceptions of mouth discomfort
title: Womens Health Screening and the Oral Microbiome

brief_summary:
Falls are a leading cause of injury-related hospitalization among older women. Age-related declines in gait speed and postural stability are known risk-factors for falls. While exercise is well-known to help maintain or improve these losses, only 24.4% of older Canadian women are considered physically active.

Dance can act as a fun and social way to engage older women in exercise. Line dancing in particular has been shown to improve gait speed, knee extensor strength and endurance; however high doses are needed to achieve gains. Clifford and colleagues found that program lengths of 24 hours are needed to effect change, while Merome and colleagues recommend 3 hours per week. These high training doses may not be feasible for participants or community centres who offer programming. The time to commute to classes, find parking and caregiver roles at home are all cited as barriers to physical activity. We also propose that BFR could be a novel addition to increase the physiologic strain of online dance classes, which we hypothesize have a lower intensity and thereby lead to less fitness adaptations. Online classes are of interest as they can serve to reduce barriers to physical activity often experienced by older adults in Canada.

* We propose online dance classes have reduced efficacy in stimulating adaptations to gait speed, strength and endurance when compared to in-person classes.
* We propose blood flow restriction (BFR) as a novel addition to dance classes in order to aid in reaching physiological overload in more efficient time-frame.

BFR works by partially reducing blood flowing in and out of working muscles, thereby reducing oxygen availability, promoting anaerobic energy pathways and keeping metabolites in the muscles for a longer time period. Numerous studies have confirmed that when combined with low-intensity exercise BFR is capable of producing similar strength gains as high-intensity exercise. Additionally, BFR is safe and has been widely used among older adults and individuals with various medical conditions, including cardiovascular conditions.

While the benefits of BFR for muscle strength and hypertrophy have been greatly studied, there is limited research on its effects on gait and postural stability. Additionally, there is minimal research on potential combinations of BFR with dance-based activity.

* This study will examine the differences between online and in-person delivery of 90 minute line dance classes on the postural stability and gait of older females over 10-weeks.
* This study will then investigate the effects of combining BFR with 10-weeks of 90 minute line dancing classes for the postural stability and gait of older females.

Finally, muscle oxygenation and kinematic analysis will be conducted to help provide insight into any potential changes in gait and postural stability.

The intervention will consist of 10-weeks of line dancing classes, during which half the groups will be randomized to wear elasticized BFR bands pulled tight to a 7/10 of perceived pressure. Classes will be once per week for 90 minutes and will include a warm-up, 4 pre-set choreographies and a cool down. Breaks will be provided throughout the class.

Assessments will occur at pre, mid and post.

Gait will be assessed during a 6-minute walk test. During the test, participants will be filmed from a sagittal view to obtain kinematics. They will also be asked to wear a heart-rate monitor and muscle oxygenation sensors on their lower limbs.

Postural stability will be assessed via 30-seconds of quiet standing on force plates in conditions of eyes open, eyes closed and foam. Participants will also be asked to wear an accelerometer on their upper back during the assessment to obtain correlation to force plate data.

Functional strength will be assessed using 30-second sit to stand (with a secondary timer to obtain 5 time sit to stand length) and the Calf-Raise Senior test. Dynamic balance and mobility will be evaluated using the Functional Reach Test, and the Timed Up and Go in both single and dual-tasks. Aerobic capacity will be measured using a 3 minute Step Test while the participant wears a heart-rate monitor and muscle oxygenation sensors.

Finally scales of fears of falling, social connectedness, and overall mental health will be collected.

It is expected that this study will have great practical implications as the accessibility of this program can provide opportunities to older adults from various remote locations to increase their levels of physical activity in a safe manner. The affordability may also aid in adoption by community health and recreation centers as an easy-to-implement program that helps to improve the postural stability and gait of older women, thereby promoting independence and quality of life.
conditions: Healthy Older Adults in the Community
title: Line Dancing With Blood Flow Restriction for Balance and Gait of Older Women (In-Person vs Online)

brief_summary:
This study looks at whether a simple blood test can help predict how well a breast cancer treatment will work. It follows patients with advanced hormone receptor-positive breast cancer whose cancer has progressed after their first treatment.

Researchers collect a blood sample when patients start a second hormone therapy treatment and may collect additional samples over time. By comparing blood test results with patient outcomes, the study aims to identify biomarkers that can predict which patients are most likely to benefit from treatment.
primary_outcomes: To Assess the performance of the baseline PERDI score
title: Blood Biomarkers for Breast Cancer Treatment Response

brief_summary:
Ischemic cardiomyopathy occurs when the heart muscle is permanently weakened due to blocked coronary arteries that limit blood flow. Current treatments, including medications and lifestyle changes, can manage symptoms but cannot restore the damaged heart muscle.

Stem cell therapy offers a promising approach to repair and regenerate damaged heart tissue. This study will evaluate the safety and tolerability of HB1011 - an allogeneic myocardium-derived mesenchymal stem cell therapy - in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy who are undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. HB1011 will be injected directly into the damaged heart muscle during the CABG procedure. Participants will receive different doses of HB1011, starting from a lower dose and gradually increasing, to identify the safest and most appropriate dose for future studies.
title: A Phase I Study of Allogeneic Myocardium-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells (HB1011) in Patients With Ischemic Cardiomyopathy

brief_summary:
Women are an underrepresented population in clinical studies on HIV and antiretroviral therapy. This study aims to help bridge this gap by providing real-world data on therapeutic management with B/F/TAF (Biktarvy) in an exclusively female cohort, aiming to improve treatment personalization and the early identification of risk factors for poor retention and treatment failure in this population.

This study is single-center, ambispective observational. The retrospective component analyzes medical record data from June 2019 (the date BIC/FTC/TAF became available in Italy) to the study data cutoff. The prospective component involves data collection during routine follow-up visits up to December 31, 2027. No diagnostic or therapeutic procedures beyond standard clinical practice are involved.

The study opulation includes adult women (≥18 years of age) with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV-1 infection who have received at least one prescription for BIC/FTC/TAF at the Infectious Diseases Unit of E.O. Ospedali Galliera in Genoa from June 2019 to the present, with a documented follow-up of at least 6 months.

The primary objective of the study is to determine the 12- and 24-month retention-in-care rates among women treated with B/F/TAF (Biktarvy) and to identify factors associated with treatment maintenance and predictors of treatment discontinuation.

Secondary objectives of the study include:

* Percentage of women achieving/maintaining virologic suppression (\<50 copies/mL) at 12 and 24 months during B/F/TAF treatment
* Evaluation of treatment persistence with B/F/TAF across different age groups
* Analysis of reasons for discontinuing B/F/TAF (adverse events, patient choice, planned switch, other)
* Identification of factors associated with virologic failure during B/F/TAF therapy
* Evaluation of the impact of menopausal status (pre- vs. post-menopause) on retention and virologic outcomes
* Analysis of the effect of the menopausal transition during follow-up on outcomes
* Correlation of past virologic history (nadir CD4, peak viremia, previous failures) with outcomes
* Evaluation of the impact of prior antiretroviral treatment history (previous lines, drug classes used, documented resistance)
* Analysis of demographic and socioeconomic variables associated with treatment persistence and virologic success
interventions: Bictegravir (BIC) plus Emtricitabine (FTC) plus Tenofovir Alafenamide (TAF)
title: Ambispective Observational Study on Retention in Care and on Clinical Chracteristics of HIV-infected Women Treated With Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Alafenamide (BIKWO).

brief_summary: This study, titled "A Randomized Controlled Trial to Evaluate the Cariostatic Efficacy of Nano Silver Fluoride (NSF) vs. Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) in Children" (Study Number: ATSU-YI-NSF 2025), is sponsored by Young Innovations and conducted at the Arizona School of Dentistry \& Oral Health (ASDOH) at A.T. Still University in Mesa, Arizona, under Principal Investigator Marc Shlossman, DDS, MS. The primary objective is to validate and compare the cariostatic efficacy of Nano Silver Fluoride (ClearDefense®) against Silver Diamine Fluoride (AdvantageArrest®) in pediatric dental patients with active carious lesions on primary molars and first permanent molars. Designed as a non-inferiority trial, it evaluates whether Nano Silver Fluoride provides comparable caries-arresting effects while assessing patient, parent, and provider acceptance, tooth color changes, and overall product safety. The trial is structured as a six-month, double-blind, parallel-group, single-site randomized controlled study with an optional twelve-month follow-up visit. To achieve a target sample size of 60 evaluable subjects (30 per treatment group) while accounting for a projected 20% dropout rate, a total of 72 pediatric participants will be recruited. Subjects are randomly assigned to treatment arms using an online random number generator. Allocation concealment and double-blinding are maintained by a third-party study coordinator who prepares treatment supplies on preset trays, keeping trial investigators, outcome examiners, and participants masked to product identity. Eligible participants include medically healthy children aged 6 to 10 years who present with at least one primary molar or permanent first molar containing active occlusal or proximal caries classified as ICDAS II Stage 3 through 6. Children and their parents or guardians must read and understand English or Spanish, provide written assent and consent, and agree to attend all required study visits. Exclusion criteria apply to children with known allergies to fluoride or silver, significant systemic conditions, ulcerative oral lesions, or conditions reducing salivary flow, as well as target teeth with loose roots, pulpal involvement, or existing restorations. At the baseline visit, active carious lesions receive a single topical application of either ClearDefense® (3% sodium fluoride + 0.2% silver ion) or AdvantageArrest® (38% silver diamine fluoride) for at least one minute. Mandatory study appointments occur at baseline, 3 months, 6 months, and an optional 12 months, incorporating clinical oral examinations, tooth cleaning, radiographs, intraoral photographs, and digital tooth shade assessments using a Vita Easyshade V spectrophotometer. The primary response variable is the clinical status of the carious lesion (active vs. arrested) measured at 3 and 6 months. Secondary outcome measures include pre- and post-treatment tooth color changes, parent-reported quality of life via the Early Childhood Oral Health Impact Scale (ECOHIS), child satisfaction regarding taste (using the TASTY scale at baseline) and tooth appearance, parent treatment acceptability, investigator ease-of-use feedback at study closeout, and documentation of adverse events including soft tissue staining or localized pain.
lead_sponsor: A.T. Still University of Health Sciences
primary_outcomes: Change in the Carious Lesion Status after Treatment
title: A Study to Evaluate the Cariostatic Efficacy of Nano Silver Fluoride (NSF) vs. Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) in Children

brief_summary:
This study will test an experimental Regeneron drug called REGN24493 hereby referred to as "study drug" to see if it can help treat Graves' disease. Graves' disease is a condition where the immune system causes the thyroid gland to make too much thyroid hormone.

The main purpose of this study is to learn about the safety of REGN24493 and what side effects it might cause.

The study is looking at:

* What side effects REGN24493 might cause
* How much REGN24493 is in the blood at different times
* How REGN24493 affects thyroid hormone levels
* If the body reacts to REGN24493 in a way that could affect participant's health
* What is the best dose of REGN24493 for treating Graves' disease
title: Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone Receptor (TSHR) Blockade With REGN24493 in Adult Participants With Graves' Disease (GD)

brief_summary: This study is a first-in-human Phase 1 clinical study conducted in healthy adult participants in China to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and immunogenicity of QLS2312 Injection after single and multiple subcutaneous administrations. The study consists of Part A and Part B: Part A is a single-ascending-dose study, and Part B is a multiple-ascending-dose (MAD) study.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Qilu Pharmaceutical Research and Development Center LTD

title: A Phase I Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Immunogenicity of QLS2312 Injection

brief_summary:
This study will assess whether methylene blue fluorescence imaging can help surgeons identify the ureters during colorectal surgery. Methylene blue, given through a vein during the operation, is taken up and excreted by the kidneys, allowing the ureters to appear under a special fluorescence camera system.

The study will include adults undergoing open, laparoscopic, or robotic colorectal surgery at Prince of Wales Hospital. The surgeons will compare ureter visibility using standard white light with visibility using fluorescence imaging at different stages of the operation. The study will also assess the best dose of methylene blue, the additional time required, the ease of using the imaging system, and whether the imaging findings affect the surgical plan.

The study's hypothesis is that methylene blue fluorescence imaging will make it easier or faster to identify the ureters than white light alone. The technique will be considered feasible if it is helpful in at least 20% of operations-for example, by identifying a ureter earlier or identifying it when it cannot be seen under white light. The findings will help determine whether a larger future study should be conducted.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of cases in which fluorescence imaging with methylene blue is deemed helpful for identifying the index ureter
title: Assessing the Feasibility of Using Methylene Blue in Identifying Ureters During Colorectal Surgery

brief_summary: This study examined an animal-assisted program for children with hematologic or oncologic disease and their siblings. The program included ten weekly sessions involving dogs and donkeys. Children allocated to the program were compared with children on a waiting list. Assessments were conducted before the program, approximately 15 days after the last session, and approximately two months after the last session. The study assessed children's reported life events, emotional indicators in human figure drawings, family relationships, and parents' coping styles. Waiting-list participants were offered the program after their own final follow-up assessment. This study is being registered retrospectively, after study completion and analysis.

Change in Parental Task-Oriented Coping: CISS Raw Score
