title: Animal-Assisted Intervention for Children With Cancer and Their Siblings

brief_summary:
This clinical trial examines the effects of guided imagery in adults recovering from laparoscopic gallbladder surgery. The study focuses on pain levels, vital signs, and the quality of recovery after surgery.

The study addresses the following questions:

* Do participants who receive guided imagery experience different levels of pain after surgery?
* Do participants' vital signs change after guided imagery?
* Does the quality of recovery differ between participants who receive guided imagery and those who do not?

Participants are followed in two groups. One group receives an 18-minute guided imagery session in addition to standard care, while the other group receives standard care only. The results from the two groups are compared to assess the possible effects of guided imagery.

During the study, participants' pain levels and vital signs are measured at planned time points. Their quality of recovery after surgery is also assessed.
primary_outcomes: Change in Postoperative Quality of Recovery
title: The Effect of Guided Imagery in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary: This study investigated whether unilateral static stretching of the quadriceps muscles produces immediate and short-term changes in muscle strength and jumping performance in both the stretched and unstretched legs. Healthy adult men performed unilateral quadriceps static stretching, and muscle strength and jumping performance were assessed before stretching and at 0, 30, 60, and 120 minutes after stretching. The study evaluated changes over time in the stretched leg and possible responses in the opposite leg.
conditions: Effects of Unilateral Quadriceps Static Stretching on Muscle Strength and Jumping Performance
title: Time Course of Responses to Unilateral Quadriceps Static Stretching

brief_summary:
The microbial profile varies between simple appendicitis (SA) and complicated appendicitis (CA) cases. An appendectomy has been noted to temporarily diminish gut bacterial diversity. Changes in the microbial profile associated with appendicitis are known to significantly influence the development of acute appendicitis (AA). Therefore accurately distinguishing between SA and CA cases is essential for selecting suitable treatment approaches.

The aim of this clinical study is to determine whether the gut bacterial profile plays a role in cases of simple and severe appendicitis in pediatric patients. Healthy volunteers will also be included in the study for the purpose of comparing results. The key questions the researchers aim to answer are:

Are there differences in the biochemical values of participants with simple versus severe appendicitis? Are there differences in the gut bacteria present in cases of simple versus severe appendicitis? There are no specific procedures or requirements for the participants or healthy volunteers to follow. There will be no changes to their treatment or medical care.
conditions: Microbiota Composition in the Human Small Intestine
primary_outcomes: Appendix tissues and rectal swabs were used for microbiota analysis and conventional cultures
Results of culture and microbiota analysis
title: Differences In Microbiota Profiles Of Pediatric Appendicitis Cases

brief_summary: This cross-sectional study aims to assess cardiovascular structural and electrophysiological alterations in obese children attending Assiut University Children's Hospital.
title: Cardiovascular Alterations in Obese Children

brief_summary: This study investigates the effectiveness of using Hololens2 for remote education and feedback in medical procedures, specifically central venous catheterization. HoloLens-based education offers realistic simulation and real-time feedback, enhancing learners' skills and providing a safe practice environment. This approach is expected to improve the efficacy of central venous catheter training and enhance healthcare professionals' abilities, thereby ensuring greater patient safety. The research aims to explore whether medical professionals can correctly perform procedures with remote guidance and feedback through Hololens2 and examines the potential of Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs) in medical education and their practical application in clinical settings.
primary_outcomes: Differences between Test and Control Group on the C-line procedure scores of pre and post test
title: Feasibility Study of an Interactive Remote Supervising Platform for Critical Care: A Randomized Study

brief_summary:
This is a monocentric study assessing hamstring and quadriceps neuromuscular fatigue after 3 consecutive soccer trainings. The purpose of this study was:

1. To quantify the difference of isometric force immediately after a simulated soccer training.
2. To characterize peripheral and central fatigue between hamstring and quadriceps muscles.
3. To compare the level neuromuscular fatigue before each session, to assess the cumulative effect of neuromuscular fatigue
4. To highlight correlation between neuromuscular fatigue and performance markers.
primary_outcomes: Pre- to Post-Exercise Change in Maximal Isometric Knee Flexor and Extensor Strength
title: Characterization of Hamstring and Quadriceps Neuromuscular Fatigue After Consecutive Soccer Trainings in Soccer Players

brief_summary:
Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Thoracic surgery remains the treatment of choice for patients with early-stage disease; however, postoperative recovery is frequently associated with reduced functional capacity, decreased physical activity levels, pulmonary complications, dyspnea, and impaired quality of life. Early physiotherapy interventions are recommended to minimize these adverse outcomes, although access to postoperative rehabilitation services remains limited in many healthcare settings, including the Andalusian Public Health System.

Telerehabilitation has emerged as a promising strategy to improve access to rehabilitation services by delivering therapeutic exercise and clinical follow-up remotely. Previous studies have demonstrated that telerehabilitation is safe, effective, and cost-efficient across different clinical populations. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness in patients recovering from lung cancer surgery remains limited.

This single-blind randomized controlled trial aims to compare the effects of an eight-week telerehabilitation program based on therapeutic exercise with usual postoperative care in patients with lung cancer undergoing thoracic surgery. Participants allocated to the intervention group will receive 24 therapeutic exercise sessions and 8 online clinical follow-up sessions delivered through the Rehbody platform over an 8-week period. Outcomes will include functional capacity, dyspnea, physical activity level, postoperative pulmonary complications, and health-related quality of life.

The study is designed to address the following research question: In adults with lung cancer undergoing thoracic surgery (Population), does an eight-week therapeutic exercise-based telerehabilitation program (Intervention), compared with usual postoperative care (Comparison), improve postoperative recovery as measured by functional capacity, dyspnea, physical activity level, postoperative pulmonary complications, and quality of life (Outcomes)?
title: Impact of a Telerehabilitation-based Therapeutic Exercise Program on Postoperative Recovery in Patients With Lung Cancer: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

brief_summary: This phase II trial tests how well Pluvicto works in treating African American patients with prostate cancer that has spread from where it first started (primary site) to other places in the body (metastatic) and that has continued to grow and spread despite the surgical removal of the testes or medical intervention to block androgen production (castration-resistant). Pluvicto is a targeted radioligand therapy. It works like a guided missile, combining tumor seeking molecules with a radioactive isotope. It circulates through the bloodstream, binds to a protein on prostate cancer cells called prostate specific membrane antigen, and destroys them using radiation. Pluvicto is approved by the Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This trial may help researchers determine the safety and efficacy of Pluvicto specifically in African American patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
conditions: Stage IVB Prostate Cancer AJCC v8
title: Pluvicto for the Treatment of African American Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to compare total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) with sevoflurane-based inhalational anesthesia in patients aged 65 years and older undergoing hip fracture surgery under general anesthesia. The study will evaluate postoperative quality of recovery using the Quality of Recovery-40 (QoR-40) questionnaire and cognitive outcomes, including postoperative delirium and cognitive status. Pain scores, opioid consumption, recovery room stay, postoperative complications, and patient satisfaction will also be recorded. The anesthesia technique will be determined by the attending anesthesiologist as part of routine clinical practice, and the researchers will not interfere with the choice of anesthesia.
lead_sponsor: Sehit Prof. Dr. Ilhan Varank Sancaktepe Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Quality of Recovery-40 (QoR-40) Score on Postoperative Day 1
title: Total Intravenous Versus Inhalational Anesthesia in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery

brief_summary: This randomized, single-blind trial compared the effects of a standardized manual therapy closure protocol, delivered alone or combined with therapeutic exercise, with therapeutic exercise alone on inter-rectus distance (IRD) in women with diastasis recti abdominis (DRA). Sixty-four participants were allocated to one of three groups: a single session of the manual protocol alone; the same protocol followed immediately by therapeutic exercise; or a group performing therapeutic exercise three times per week for three months without the manual protocol. IRD was measured by ultrasound at three abdominal levels, under passive and active conditions, at diagnostic assessment (baseline), immediately after the intervention (manual therapy groups only), and after three months. Secondary outcomes included trunk mobility, respiratory chest excursion, and waist circumference.
interventions: Therapeutic Exercise for Deep Abdominal Activation
title: Manual Therapy for Diastasis Recti Abdominis

brief_summary:
Adults with type 1 diabetes have elevated cardiovascular disease risk, and systolic blood pressure is a leading modifiable contributor to that risk. Aerobic exercise lowers blood pressure but poses time and glycemic-management barriers for people with type 1 diabetes. Inspiratory muscle strength training is a brief, home-based, device-based intervention that takes about five minutes per day and has lowered systolic blood pressure in other adult populations.

This pilot trial will test whether eight weeks of daily high-resistance inspiratory muscle strength training lowers blood pressure and improves vascular function in adults with type 1 diabetes. Participants will be randomized 2:1 to high-resistance or very-low-resistance sham training using a POWERbreathe K3 device and will complete 30 training breaths per day at home for eight weeks. Outcomes are assessed before and after the training period.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Laboratory-Measured Seated Systolic Blood Pressure at 8 Weeks
title: Inspiratory Muscle Strength Training in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the effectiveness and postoperative outcomes of quilting suture and chain suture techniques in patients undergoing septoplasty for symptomatic deviated nasal septum. The study will include patients older than 15 years undergoing septoplasty.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does quilting suture or chain suture result in a shorter suture placement/surgical duration?
* Is there a difference between the two techniques in postoperative pain, bleeding, septal hematoma, and adhesions/synechiae formation?

Researchers will compare patients receiving quilting sutures with patients receiving chain sutures to evaluate differences in surgical duration and postoperative complications. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups.

Participants will:

* Undergo septoplasty as part of their planned treatment.
* Be randomly assigned to receive either quilting suture or chain suture to close and stabilize the nasal septum.
* Have postoperative pain assessed using a visual analog scale on postoperative days 1, 2, and 3.
* Be assessed for postoperative bleeding and septal hematoma.
* Be examined for adhesions/synechiae on postoperative day 15 and at 1 month.
lead_sponsor: Services Institute of Medical Sciences, Pakistan
title: Quilting Versus Chain Suture in Septoplasty

brief_summary: As a profession, law enforcement produces unique occupational health outcomes for officers and civilians. To date, most studies have focused on improving health outcomes related to law enforcement from a microlevel perspective, with particular attention to individual and behavioral factors. Such a focus misses the broader macro-level factors that perpetuate occupational harms. To address this gap, this study uses the PRECEDE-PROCEED model of intervention development to examine modifiable macro-level factors contributing to adverse occupational health outcomes for law enforcement and civilians. Using a mixed-method design and partnering with local law enforcement agencies, the investigators will implement and test an intervention to reduce occupational health harms related to law enforcement.

brief_summary: Each year over 795,000 people suffer from stroke resulting in the primary cause of adult disability. Persistent upper limb dysfunction due to stroke significantly impairs performance and results in a serious decline of quality of life. As most daily activities involve the use of both arms, restoring the coordination between upper limbs is essential for regaining functional independence. Only a few interventions have been designed for improving function of both arms, and most of these interventions have focused on movement retraining without directly facilitating the injured brain. The purpose of this study is to design and test a noninvasive brain stimulation protocol tailored to enhance the coordination between the arms in individuals with chronic stroke. The investigators propose that the dorsal premotor cortex on the noninjured side of the brain (cPMd) could serve as a potential stimulation target for enhancing arm coordination and brain function. In the first part of this study (Aim 1), the investigators will examine its effects on modulating arm movements in individuals with chronic stroke. In the second part of this study (Aim 2), the investigators will upregulate the activity of the most responsive region (cPMd or iM1) of each participant prior to arm movement training (bilateral arm training, BAT) to determine the combined effects on augmenting bilateral arm coordination and brain function in individuals with chronic stroke.
interventions: 5 Hz Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on the contralesional dorsal premotor cortex (cPMd)
5 Hz Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on the ipsilesional primary motor cortex (iM1)
primary_outcomes: Cortical Excitability Assessed by Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS)-Induced Motor Evoked Potential (MEP) Amplitude
Interlimb Coordination Assessed by Surface Electromyography (EMG) -Interlimb Muscle Coherence
Arm Reaching Kinematics (Speed, Acceleration, Interlimb Coordination, and Trajectory Smoothness) Assessed by the 3D Kinesiological Instrument for Normal and Altered Reaching Movement (KINARM)
title: Optimizing Cortical Priming

brief_summary:
SBO-CHOICE\*\* is a prospective, multicenter observational study investigating the management of \*\*adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO), a condition in which scar tissue (adhesions), usually resulting from previous abdominal surgery, causes a blockage of the small intestine.

Adhesive small bowel obstruction is a common reason for emergency hospital admission. In patients who do not have signs of bowel ischemia, strangulation, peritonitis, or other conditions requiring immediate surgery, treatment may initially be non-operative. This can include intravenous fluids, temporary fasting, placement of a nasogastric tube when needed, and the use of water-soluble contrast agents. Many patients recover without an operation. However, some patients eventually require surgery, and bowel obstruction may recur after discharge.At present, it remains uncertain which treatment strategy provides the best long-term outcomes for patients in whom surgery is considered a reasonable option but is not immediately necessary.

1. What is the purpose of the study? The main purpose of SBO-CHOICE is to compare the outcomes of adult patients admitted with adhesive small bowel obstruction who are treated: with surgery during their initial hospital admission, or with non-operative (medical) management and discharged without surgery. The primary outcome is whether patients are readmitted to hospital because of another episode of adhesive small bowel obstruction within 12 months. The study will also examine other important outcomes, including the need for emergency surgery during follow-up, complications, mortality, length of hospital stay, further adhesion-related procedures, and patients' quality of life.
2. Does participation determine which treatment a patient receives? SBO-CHOICE is an observational study and does not assign patients to a particular treatment.All diagnostic and treatment decisions are made by the treating surgical team according to the patient's clinical condition and normal clinical practice. Participation in the study does not require doctors to change their usual treatment or follow a study-specific treatment algorithm.

   The researchers will observe and compare what happens to patients who receive the different treatment strategies in real-world clinical practice.
3. Who can participate? The study includes adults aged 18 years or older who are admitted urgently to participating hospitals with a clinical and CT-confirmed diagnosis of adhesive small bowel obstruction.Patients who require immediate emergency surgery, including those with signs of bowel ischemia, strangulation, peritonitis, hemodynamic instability, or other serious complications, are not included in the study. Other exclusion criteria are specified in the study protocol.
4. What happens after enrollment? Clinical information regarding the initial hospital admission and the treatment received will be collected. After discharge, patients will be followed by telephone at approximately 30 days, 90 days, 6 months, and annually thereafter for up to 5 years.

   During follow-up, researchers will collect information about complications, further hospital admissions, recurrent bowel obstruction, additional procedures or operations, and other relevant clinical outcomes. Quality of life will also be assessed using validated questionnaires.
5. Are there additional risks from participating? Because SBO-CHOICE is observational, participation does not introduce an experimental treatment or alter routine clinical management. Treatment-related risks are therefore those associated with the medical or surgical care that the patient would receive independently of participation in the study.

   Patients will receive detailed information about the study before enrollment and will be asked to provide written informed consent. Participation is voluntary, and patients may withdraw their consent at any time without affecting the quality of their medical care.
6. How will personal information be protected? Clinical and study data will be collected in a secure electronic database. Patient-identifying information such as names, addresses, telephone numbers, or dates of birth will not be entered into the study database. Study data will be pseudonymized using an alphanumeric code and managed according to appropriate confidentiality and data-protection procedures.

   Results may be presented at scientific meetings or published in scientific journals, but only in aggregated or anonymous form so that individual participants cannot be identified.
7. Why is this study important? Although non-operative treatment is successful in many patients with adhesive small bowel obstruction, recurrence remains an important clinical problem. Surgery may reduce the risk of future obstruction in selected patients, but it also carries operative risks and may itself lead to the formation of new adhesions.The study want to provide better evidence about the short- and long-term outcomes of these patients.
title: Management of Non Emergency Adhesive Small Bowel Obstruction:

brief_summary: This clinical study is being conducted to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of zenagamtide in people with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and excess body weight compared with placebo. The purpose of this clinical study is to find out if zenagamtide is safe and effective for treating people who have ASCVD and excess body weight. Participants will be randomly assigned by chance to receive either zenagamtide, the investigational treatment being tested, or a placebo, which contains no active medicine. Half of the participants will receive zenagamtide, and treatment assignment will be determined randomly. Zenagamtide is a new investigational medicine that is not yet available for prescription by doctors.
primary_outcomes: Time from randomization to first occurrence of a 4-point (P) composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) endpoint consisting of: Cardiovascular (CV) death, Non-fatal MI, Non-fatal stroke, HF hospitalization or urgent HF visit
title: A Research Study to Look at How Well Zenagamtide Works Compared to Placebo in People With Established Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease and Either Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary: Patients with chronic masticatory myofascial pain (MFP) often report that stress and parafunctional oral habits aggravate their pain, consistent with the widespread belief that stress and parafunctional habits lead to increased/sustained jaw muscle activity and subsequent pain. Yet, these assumptions have never been directly tested, given the lack of tools to measure masticatory muscle activity in real-world settings. This protocol describes a prospective, longitudinal, case-control observational study that will enroll 50 patients total (25 with clinician-diagnosed chronic MFP and 25 age- and sex-matched healthy controls) from the university-based dental clinics at Midwestern University, Illinois. Consenting participants will be instructed to complete a baseline biopsychosocial battery assessing self-reported awake and sleep bruxism (using the Oral Behavior Checklist, OBC), anxiety/depression symptoms (using the Patient Health Questionnaire, PHQ-4), perceived stress (using the Perceived Stress Scale, PSS), insomnia symptoms (using the Insomnia Severity Index, ISI) and chronic pain intensity (using the Graded Chronic Pain Scale, GCPS). All participants will be provided a 24-hour electromyograph (EMG) device (dia-BRUXO, Biotech-Novations, Sanremo, Italy) placed on the left masseter, recording jaw muscle activity. Brief ecological momentary assessments will be sent during the 24-hour period, assessing pain intensity, self-reported parafunctional habits, stress and anxiety. The primary aim will be to establish if self-reported awake and sleep bruxism and/or biopsychosocial distress are as-sociated with EMG-recorded masticatory muscle activity. The secondary aim will test if masticatory muscle activity is associated with jaw pain intensity.
title: Masticatory Muscle Activity Using a 24-Hour Wearable Device

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn more about how adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer patients, their parents and caregivers (referred to as a carebuddy in this study), and their healthcare providers think about and communicate around vaping and tobacco use. We hope this information will help us develop educational materials and provider training tools that are appropriate for young people with cancer.

A Community Advisory Board that is made up of AYA patients, parents/caregivers, and healthcare providers, is helping to guide the study. The board will review the materials, give feedback, help the study team understand the findings, and provides input to make sure the study is appropriate and practical for participants.
primary_outcomes: support needs to inform the development of developmentally appropriate vaping cessation resources.
title: Study of Vaping Use Among Adolescent and Young Adult Patients With Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to develop and evaluate an MRI-based assessment system for predicting neurodevelopmental outcomes in infants with punctate white matter lesions (PWML). This is a multicenter, bidirectional cohort study that includes both a retrospective cohort identified from existing clinical and imaging databases and a prospective cohort of consecutively enrolled participants. The study aims to better understand how MRI findings are associated with later developmental outcomes and to identify imaging markers that may help stratify developmental risk.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Which MRI features are associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in infants with PWML?
2. Can MRI-based quantitative assessment methods provide early risk stratification for neurodevelopmental outcomes in infants with PWML?

Participants with PWML diagnosed by brain MRI will be followed and evaluated for neurodevelopmental outcomes. Researchers will analyze clinical information and MRI findings collected from participants to develop and validate prediction models. Participants will:

1. undergo brain MRI examinations according to clinical protocols;
2. receive standardized neurodevelopmental assessments during follow-up;
3. have their MRI findings and developmental outcomes analyzed to identify factors associated with later neurodevelopment.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital Xi'an Jiaotong University
title: MRI-Based Neurodevelopmental Risk Stratification in Infants With White Matter Injury

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial will compare oral furosemide with placebo for improving blood pressure control in women with severe preeclampsia after delivery. Participants will receive either 20 mg of furosemide or a placebo tablet once daily for 5 days, in addition to standard postpartum treatment for high blood pressure. Blood pressure, symptoms, adverse events, and the need for additional antihypertensive medication will be monitored for 7 days after delivery. The study will assess whether adding furosemide helps achieve better postpartum blood pressure control compared with placebo.
title: Role of Postpartum Furosemide in Recovery of Patients With Severe Preeclampsia

brief_summary: This observational study will examine the relationships among diabetes distress, practical barriers to medication use, diabetes self-management, and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes. Participants who meet the study criteria and agree to take part will complete questionnaires about their personal and clinical characteristics, diabetes distress, medication-taking barriers, and diabetes self-management. With their permission, the most recent HbA1c result measured within the previous three months will be obtained from their medical record. No treatment or medication changes will be made for this study. The researchers plan to include at least 137 participants.
primary_outcomes: Glycemic control measured by glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c)
title: Diabetes Distress, Medication Adherence Barriers, Self-Management, and Glycemic Control in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to evaluate whether the School of Caring programme improves quality of life and reduces caregiver burden among informal carers of people living with dementia. The study will also examine how the programme is implemented in primary care settings and assess its economic efficiency.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does participation in the School of Caring programme improve the quality of life of informal carers of people with dementia? Does the programme reduce the negative impact and burden associated with caregiving? What factors facilitate or hinder the implementation of the programme in primary care centres? Is the programme cost-utility compared with usual care?

Researchers will compare informal carers who participate in the programme with carers who receive usual care.

Participants will:

Take part in nine face-to-face group sessions (one every two weeks) delivered in primary care centres.

Receive health education, information about social and community resources, practical guidance for daily care, physiotherapy and nutritional support, and strategies to promote self-care and emotional well-being.

Share experiences with other carers and participate in peer support activities. Complete study assessments to measure quality of life, caregiver burden and other relevant outcomes throughout the study period.

brief_summary: Doctors spend much of each visit collecting the patient's medical history, and incomplete histories can delay diagnosis. This study tests an AI chatbot that interviews patients before their appointment and produces a structured summary of their history for the doctor. Adult patients at the first study site, a university gynecology outpatient clinic in Germany, answer the chatbot's questions on a tablet before the doctor visit. The doctor then takes the history and examines the patient as usual, without seeing the chatbot's output. Only after the doctor has finished planning care does the doctor review the chatbot's summary and rate its usefulness and accuracy. The chatbot does not change patient care. Patients also rate the ease of use and acceptability of the chatbot. The investigators will report how useful doctors find the summaries, how complete and correct the summaries are, and how patients experience the tool.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out whether personalized, non-invasive brain stimulation can temporarily change communication within brain networks related to restrictive eating in adults with anorexia nervosa.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does personalized transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) change functional connectivity within a brain network related to restrictive eating compared with sham stimulation?
* Do different types of TMS affect measures related to inhibitory control, body image, eating-disorder symptoms, mood, and anxiety, and are they safe and well tolerated?

Participants will:

* Attend four study visits, separated by at least one week.
* Complete clinical and psychological assessments and undergo brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
* Receive three stimulation conditions in random order at separate visits: intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS), continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS), and sham stimulation.
* Complete brain MRI scans and research tasks so that the effects of the three stimulation conditions can be compared.

Researchers will compare the effects of iTBS and cTBS with sham stimulation on brain connectivity and other study measures.

This is an exploratory proof-of-concept study designed to test whether personalized brain stimulation can engage the targeted brain circuit. It is not designed to determine whether TMS is an effective treatment for anorexia nervosa, and direct clinical benefit to participants is not expected.
primary_outcomes: Post-Stimulation Target-to-Network Resting-State fMRI Functional Connectivity
title: Circuit-Guided Neuromodulation for Anorexia Nervosa

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to find out whether a web-based simulation with game features helps first-year nursing students learn how to give an injection into the muscle on the side of the hip, known as the ventrogluteal site. The study will compare this approach with traditional teaching at Cankiri Karatekin University in Türkiye.

The main questions are whether the web-based simulation improves students' knowledge and practical skills, increases their satisfaction and confidence in learning, and helps them remember what they have learned after eight weeks.

All participants will receive the same initial classroom teaching and laboratory demonstration. They will then be assigned by chance to one of two groups. One group will receive traditional teaching. The other group will use the web-based simulation, which includes a patient scenario and interactive tasks, such as selecting equipment and moving items to a tray.

The simulation has two modes. In the learning mode, students receive hints and explanations without being scored. In the self-test mode, they complete tasks without hints and receive a score report for feedback. Students must answer correctly before moving to the next step.

Participants will complete a knowledge test, a practical skills assessment using an injection training model, and a questionnaire about satisfaction and confidence before the group-specific training and again one week afterward. They will repeat the knowledge test eight weeks after training to assess how much they remember. Practical skills will be assessed by two observers who do not know which teaching group each student belongs to.
conditions: Ventrogluteal Injection Training in Nursing Students
title: Web-Based Gamified Simulation for Teaching Ventrogluteal Injection to First-Year Nursing Students

This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial evaluated the effectiveness of high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) in patients with early-stage symptomatic knee osteoarthritis.

A total of 39 participants were randomly assigned to receive either HILT combined with a standardized home exercise program or sham laser therapy combined with the same exercise program. Laser or sham treatment was administered over 10 weekday sessions during a two-week period.

Participants were assessed at baseline, immediately after treatment, and at the three-month follow-up. Assessments included pain intensity, physical function, health-related quality of life, walking performance, knee range of motion, and muscle strength.

The aim was to determine whether adding HILT to exercise provides additional clinical benefits compared with sham laser therapy combined with exercise.

brief_summary:
The increase in vitamin A deficiency (\<20 mcg/dL) among children under five in Colombia (2010-2015) is a public health problem (27.3%). The objective of this randomized, controlled, double-blind clinical trial was to determine whether daily consumption of retinol-fortified sugar (23.5 mcg ER/day) was effective in treating this deficiency in children; furthermore, to evaluate whether daily sugar consumption (13 g/day) increased excess weight (P/T: overweight and obesity) in them.

The main questions were:

* Does daily consumption of retinol-fortified sugar (23.5 mcg ER/g) significantly increase serum retinol levels in children in the intervention group during the study?
* What is the increase in weight-for-height among study participants at the end of the intervention following daily consumption of sugar in various meals throughout the day? The researchers compared daily consumption of retinol-fortified sugar over three months with daily consumption of regular sugar or a placebo to determine whether the fortified sugar was effective in increasing serum retinol levels in children in the intervention group and, furthermore, whether the increase in weight-for-height among participants at the end of the study showed no statistically significant differences compared to baseline.

Participants were required to:

* Children undergo antiparasitic treatment at each school with 400 mg of albendazole before starting the sugar intervention, in the presence of a nutritionist from the team.
* The nutritionist be able to assess the children's anthropometric indicators at the beginning and end of the study to evaluate changes in the presence of undernutrition or excess weight (overweight and obesity).
* Caregivers must allow the collection of two 5-ml blood samples: the first to assess baseline serum levels of retinol and CRP before the intervention; and the second and final sample at the end of the intervention to measure the levels of retinol and CRP achieved during the study through the consumption of retinol-fortified sugar.
* Caregivers would provide baseline information on the consumption of food groups (at baseline: semiquantitative frequency of consumption; and at baseline and at the end of the study: 24-hour dietary recalls). In addition, they would provide information at three different time points on the semiquantitative consumption of supplements and foods that are sources of vitamin A and carotenoids.
* Caregivers and teachers will provide the nutritionist with information at baseline, during the intervention, and at the end of the study regarding the presence of infectious diseases, clinical signs of infection and their duration, as well as the occurrence of adverse events among participants who consumed fortified sugar (13 g/day: 23.5 mcg ER/g).
interventions: refined white sugar for culinary use
primary_outcomes: Effect of consuming retinol-fortified sugar on serum levels in children of both sexes aged 3 to 6 years
title: Effect of Consuming Vitamin A-fortified Sugar on Serum Retinol Levels in Children

brief_summary:
Lung cancer is common and serious, but when detected early, the chances of recovery are significantly better. Tobacco use is the leading cause. To help people break free from smoking, the Fribourg Cantonal Hospital (HFR), the Center for Tobacco Prevention (CIPRET), and the Fribourg Cancer League are joining forces in the STOP-LungCancer study (Smoking Termination Outcomes with Pulmonary Low Dose Computed Tomography for Lung Cancer Screening).

What is the goal of this study? The investigators want to determine whether seeing and understanding images of the participants' own lungs helps participants quit smoking for good. Smoking cessation will be verified at 6 months using a breath test (measuring carbon monoxide), followed by a 2-year follow-up.

How does participation work? The study is open to 116 residents of the canton of Fribourg aged 50 to 79 who are heavy smokers and motivated to quit.

The program includes:

1. Personalized support: 4 smoking cessation coaching sessions organized by CIPRET.
2. Lung computed tomography (CT) scans: 3 exams spaced one year apart. This scan involves no needles or injections. The radiation dose is very low, about 0.6 millisieverts (mSv) per scan, and the associated risk is considered very low.
3. A review of the images with a doctor: During dedicated consultations, a thoracic radiologist reviews the participant's own computed tomography (CT) scans with the participant to explain the condition of the lungs and heart.

What are the benefits? Participants receive both tailored support to quit smoking and close monitoring to detect any potential issues at a very early stage.
title: Impact of Lung Cancer Screening With Chest Scans Combined With Coaching on Smoking Cessation in Heavy Smokers

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to learn whether adding neurofeedback therapy to cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)-based psychoeducation could reduce test anxiety in university students more than CBT-based psychoeducation alone.

The main questions it aimed to answer were:

1. Did adding neurofeedback to CBT-based psychoeducation produce a greater reduction in test anxiety than CBT-based psychoeducation alone?
2. Did test anxiety levels change from before the intervention to the middle and end of the intervention period?

Researchers compared two groups. One group received CBT-based psychoeducation together with neurofeedback training, while the other group received CBT-based psychoeducation alone. Participants were randomly assigned to one of the two groups.

Participants:

* Completed screening for test anxiety using the Westside Test Anxiety Scale (WTAS).
* Completed the Test Anxiety Inventory (TAI) before, during, and after the intervention.
* Received CBT-based psychoeducation on test anxiety and coping strategies.
* Participants assigned to the neurofeedback group also completed a baseline EEG assessment and received 10 sessions of EEG-based neurofeedback training targeting high-beta2 activity at the F4 electrode site.
* Practised CBT-based coping strategies during the intervention period.

The main outcome was change in Test Anxiety Inventory scores across the three assessment points and whether the pattern of change differed between the two study groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in Test Anxiety Inventory (TAI) Total Score Across Pre-, Mid-, and Post-Intervention
title: Neurofeedback Therapy Added to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy-Based Psychoeducation for Test Anxiety Among Undergraduate Students: A Randomised Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), previously known as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, is an increasingly recognized comorbidity in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Chronic low-grade inflammation, altered lipid metabolism, and certain antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens may heighten the vulnerability of people living with HIV (PLWH) to liver fat accumulation, progressive liver fibrosis, and cardiometabolic complications.

The primary purpose of this observational case-control study is to determine the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and laboratory findings of MASLD and hepatic fibrosis among PLWH compared with matched HIV-negative individuals. The study also aims to evaluate dietary quality, lifestyle habits, and cardiovascular risk profiles in both groups, and to determine whether adherence to a healthy lifestyle protects against significant liver disease.

Adult participants (aged 18 years and older) attending the Department of Tropical Medicine and Gastroenterology at Assiut University Hospitals will be enrolled into two groups: people living with HIV and HIV-negative individuals matched by age, sex, and degree of liver steatosis.

All participants will complete the following non-invasive evaluations:

* Hepatic Assessment: Abdominal ultrasound and transient elastography (FibroScan) to detect fatty liver and quantify liver stiffness, alongside non-invasive scoring systems (FIB-4 score and NAFLD Fibrosis Score).
* Laboratory Investigations: Fasting blood tests including liver function tests, lipid profiles, glycemic status (HbA1c), kidney function, complete blood count, and immune markers (CD4+ T-cell count and CD4/CD8 ratio).
* Physical and Body Measurements: Measurement of body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, and mid-arm muscle circumference (MAMC).
* Dietary and Lifestyle Questionnaires: Validated assessment tools including the Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ), Short Healthy Eating Index (sHEI), and Healthy Lifestyle Questionnaire to quantify nutritional quality, physical activity, and daily lifestyle habits.
* Cardiometabolic Risk Calculation: Calculation of predicted cardiovascular risk using the American Heart Association PREVENT risk score.

Findings from this study are intended to clarify the role of dietary quality and lifestyle factors in liver and metabolic health among people living with HIV, potentially informing proactive screening and management strategies.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)
title: Lifestyle, Dietary Patterns, and Cardiometabolic Risk in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Among People Living With HIV

brief_summary:
Background: Haemophilic arthropathy is associated with chronic pain, functional limitation and impaired quality of life. Pain interference may also be influenced by cognitive, emotional and behavioural factors. Evidence for structured multicomponent pain self-management programmes specifically tailored to adults with haemophilic arthropathy remains limited.

Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of a structured multicomponent pain self-management programme, compared with usual care, in reducing pain interference in adults with haemophilia A or B, haemophilic arthropathy and chronic pain.

Methods: Approximately 70 adults will be individually randomised in a 1:1 ratio to a multicomponent pain self-management programme or usual care. The intervention will comprise three 60-minute face-to-face group sessions delivered over approximately 6-8 weeks. The programme will integrate pain education, emotional-regulation training and cognitive-behavioural self-management strategies. Assessments will be performed at baseline, immediately after the intervention and at 6 months. The primary outcome will be the between-group difference in change in Brief Pain Inventory-Interference score from baseline to 6 months.
primary_outcomes: Change in pain interference from baseline to 6 months
title: Multicomponent Pain Self-Management in Adults With Haemophilic Arthropathy

brief_summary:
Sjögren's syndrome is an autoimmune disease.

Dry syndrome is a key feature of this condition, almost always leading to dryness of the mouth and eyes. It manifests as a decrease in the production of saliva and tears, causing discomfort for patients. This chronic dryness contributes to oral and ocular conditions.

It is caused by lymphocytic infiltration of the exocrine glands, leading to their inflammation and subsequent fibrosis, which results in a decrease in fluid production by these glands.

This chronic inflammation causes fatigue in the patient. Furthermore, in 30 to 60% of cases, Sjögren's syndrome may involve extra-glandular involvement, most commonly affecting the joints, but also involving the lungs, nervous system, and kidneys. Additionally, patients with thisdisease have a higher risk of developing lymphoma compared to unaffected individuals.

The current treatment for Sjögren's syndrome is the same as that for dry eye syndrome; it is primarily symptomatic, involving lifestyle and dietary changes, the use of eye drops or oral lubricants, and medication to stimulate saliva production. To date, there is no medication available to treat Sjögren's syndrome and thus the cause of dry eye syndrome.

In our laboratory (INSERM 1098, UMR Right), we have developed cells that suppress the immune system (immunosuppressive cells) derived from human monocytes cultured ex vivo using a patented process called HuMoSC (Human Monocyte -derived Suppressor Cells). These cells possess strong immunosuppressive capacity, already demonstrated in vitro and in vivo in mouse models.

The aim of this study is to evaluate whether HuMoSCs can reduce the accumulation of immune cells and thereby decrease chronic inflammation and, in the longer term, limit the development of fibrosis (hardening with tissue destruction and scarring) in the salivary glands.

Biopsy of the accessory salivary glands is already part of the diagnostic process for Sjögren's syndrome. During this biopsy, additional accessory salivary glands will be collected and sent to the laboratory for this study. These glands will be cultured in the presence of HuMoSC supernatant, and the impact of this treatment will be analyzed.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of the various subclasses of lymphocytes and macrophages
Concentrations of inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines in the culture supernatants of accessory salivary glands cultured with or without HuMoSC supernatant.
title: Exploratory Study of the Efficacy of HuMoSCs (Human Monocyte-derived Suppressor Cells) on Glandular Involvement in Sjögren's Syndrome

brief_summary:
Infertility affects about one in seven couples in France. Beyond the medical and personal challenges, it has major societal implications. In vitro fertilization (IVF) offers hope to these couples, but success rates remain modest (about 30% per embryo transfer). The failure of embryo implantation is multifactorial. Among the factors involved, immune status at the time of embryo transfer plays a central role. Embryo transfer induces an acute pro-inflammatory immune response, and inadequate regulation of this response could compromise implantation.

We have previously identified a promising immune biomarker: TGF-β (Transforming Growth Factor Beta). In a prospective cohort of 255 patients undergoing frozen embryo transfer, we demonstrated that low circulating levels of TGF-β following nonspecific stimulation of immune cells on the day of embryo transfer were associated with a significant increase in the likelihood of implantation and live birth.

These results now require independent validation in a new cohort to establish their robustness and explore potential clinical applications. We hypothesize that measuring TGF-β concentration following stimulation can predict the success of embryo implantation.
title: Low TGF-β and Embryo Implantation in the Context of Assisted Reproductive Technology: Confirmation of a Biomarker Predictive of Success and Characterization of the Immune Microenvironment.

brief_summary: Pediatric patients, hospitalization in a pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) is not merely a situation requiring physical treatment, but also an experience that has significant psychosocial effects. This project was designed to evaluate the effect of a mood journal intervention on anxiety levels, mindfulness, and emotion regulation skills in conscious pediatric patients aged 9-14 years in a pediatric intensive care unit. An emotion journal is a supportive tool that allows children to express the experiences they have during the day, the emotions they feel, and their reactions to these emotions in a structured format. It is anticipated that this practice may help children develop their abilities to recognize, express, and regulate their emotions; it may also reduce their anxiety levels related to the intensive care process. Children admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit who are conscious, able to communicate, and meet the inclusion criteria will be assigned to the intervention and control groups using a randomization method. At the start of the study, both groups will be provided with the Child and Parent Information Form, the Child and Adolescent Mindfulness Scale, the Emotion Regulation Scale for Children and Adolescents, and the State Anxiety Scale for Children will be administered to both groups. The intervention group will participate in an emotion journaling program for 5 days, approximately 30 minutes per day, while the control group will receive routine clinical care. Data will be analyzed using the SPSS 30.0 statistical software; descriptive statistics, normality tests, parametric or non-parametric group comparison tests, and correlation analyses will be performed. As a result of the project, it is expected that the emotion journaling intervention will reduce children's anxiety levels, increase their mindfulness, and support their emotion regulation skills. It is anticipated that the findings will contribute to the development of implementable, low-cost, and child-centered psychosocial care interventions in pediatric intensive care units.
title: Emotion Diary Application

brief_summary:
Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS) is a rare autoimmune disorder, characterized by: a) incapacitating diffuse muscle stiffness prominent in the axial, abdominal and thoracolumbar paraspinal muscles leading to hyperlordosis, difficulty turning and bending; b) painful muscle spasms precipitated by external stimuli with difficulty performing routine daily activities; and c) slow freezing gait with frequent falls and need for walking aids leading to disability. SPS is due to impaired inhibitory GABAergic neurotransmission associated with high-titer IgG antibodies against Glutamic Acid Decarboxylase (GAD), the rate-limiting enzyme for the synthesis of the inhibitory gammaaminobutyric acid (GABA). Although SPS patients respond to IVIg based on the PI's controlled study (NEJM 2001), several patients do not improve, or their response is modest and declines over time, as documented in a longitudinal study of 36 patients followed in our Jefferson clinic; because another controlled study we performed with Rituximab was negative and SPS is a progressive disease, new therapies are needed. Efgartigimod is an FcRn inhibitor that enhances the catabolism of circulating IgG; its subcutaneous, self-administered form, HYTRULO, has been effective and FDA-approved in patients with myasthenia gravis or CIDP poorly responding to IVIg. There is evidence that patients with myasthenia who also had SPS, Hytrulo not only helped their myasthenia but the SPS also impressively improved.

The present study is an investigator- initiated, double-blind, placebo controlled, cross-over, trial in 26 GAD-positive SPS patients poorly responding to available therapies. Patients will be recruited from the large number of patients seen and referred to the PI who is known for his work in SPS and has conducted the 2 previous controlled trials. Although Hytrulo is approved as selfadministered subcutaneous drug with pre-refilled syringes, in this study will be given by a contracted home infusion company once a week to ensure convenience, safety and validity. Patients will be randomized by the Jefferson Pharmacy to receiving Hytrulo or identical hyaluronidase-containing placebo for 3 months; then they will be crossed-over to placebo/Hytrulo for another 3 months. Efficacy will be based on one primary endpoint, the stiffness index, previously validated by the PI, and on two also validated secondary endpoints of time to walk and excitability index. This design provides the statistical power to objectively assess a 25-50% or greater change and objectively determine if Hytrulo offers meaningful benefits in reducing stiffness and spasms, improving gait and increasing quality of life in SPS patients poorly responding to current therapies.
title: VYVGART (Hytrulo) in Patients With Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS)

brief_summary: This study examined whether adding an oral magnesium supplement to behavioral counseling reduced pain in adults with chronic jaw muscle pain. Fifty adults were randomly assigned to two groups. One group received magnesium citrate providing 200 mg of elemental magnesium daily for 30 days and behavioral counseling. The other group received behavioral counseling alone. Pain, jaw movement, jaw function, pain-related disability, and anxiety were assessed before treatment and at 1 and 3 months. The main outcome was jaw muscle pain intensity at 3 months. Adverse events were also recorded. The study was completed before registration.
title: Magnesium Citrate in Chronic Masticatory Myofascial Pain

brief_summary:

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial compared two methods of attaching orthodontic brackets to teeth: conventional direct bonding, in which each bracket is placed and bonded individually in the mouth, and a segmented modified indirect bonding technique, in which brackets are first positioned on a plaster model of the patient's teeth and then transferred to the mouth in segments using a hot-glue transfer tray. The purpose was to find out whether the two techniques differ in how often brackets come loose (bond failure) during treatment.

Eighteen patients receiving fixed orthodontic appliances at Riyadh Elm University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, were randomly assigned so that their brackets were placed by either the direct or the modified indirect technique. The same bracket type and adhesive were used in both groups. Patients were examined every four weeks for six months, and any bracket that debonded was recorded along with the tooth involved, the arch (upper or lower), the side (right or left), and the time from bonding to failure. The main outcome was the time from bonding to bracket failure; the investigators also compared failure rates and examined whether failure varied by tooth type, arch, or side.
primary_outcomes: Time to bracket bond failure (time to debond)
title: Segmented Indirect Versus Direct Bracket Bonding

brief_summary:
The tongue plays a key role in maintaining upper airway patency during sleep, mainly through the genioglossus, the principal pharyngeal dilator muscle. Its dysfunction may be linked to the development of obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (oSDB), a condition affecting more than one in ten children and associated with cardiovascular and cognitive consequences. Although adenotonsillectomy remains the treatment of choice, it fails in a substantial proportion of cases because of persistent obstruction at other sites, the tongue base being involved in one third of these cases. Therefore, a better characterization of the tongue in children with oSDB is needed, since the extent to which its structure and function contribute to upper airway obstruction in this population remains largely unknown.

Our team has established the reproducibility of tongue function measurements in healthy children and is currently building a reference database. What is still lacking is an assessment of tongue structure and function in children with oSDB. Such data would allow comparison with healthy children, thereby improving the understanding of oSDB pathophysiology and informing clinical management.

Primary objective: To describe tongue structure and function in children with oSDB.

Secondary objective: To compare tongue structure and function between children with oSDB and healthy children, using data from a previous study conducted in healthy children (TMAC study, UCLouvain).
title: Characterization of the Tongue in Children With Obstructive Sleep-disordered Breathing

brief_summary:
The Haemato Oncology Foundation for Adults in the Netherlands (HOVON) has designed this study. Researchers (all doctors) are conducting the study at various hospitals in the Netherlands, Denmark and Sweden.

The study medicines pirtobrutinib and epcoritamab that are used in this study are made available by pharmaceutical companies Eli Lilly and AbbVie. This study is also funded by AbbVie and Eli Lilly.

HOVON needs 70 participants for this study.

The purpose of this study is to find out how safe and effective the combination of pirtobrutinib tablets and subcutaneous epcoritamab is for patients with CLL whose disease has come back after previous treatment or whose disease did not respond well to the previous treatment. The goal is to suppress the CLL to such an extent that the disease does not come back for a long time.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate efficacy in terms of Progression-free survival (PFS)
title: Treatment of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia or Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma With Pirtobrutinib in Combination With Epcoritamab if the Disease Comes Back After Previous Treatment.

brief_summary: This study aims to examine whether the posture of the upper back (thoracic kyphosis) is related to body awareness, core stability, and balance in people who regularly participate in weightlifting. Participants will undergo assessments of thoracic posture, proprioception, core stability, and dynamic balance. The study will also compare these measurements between different groups of weightlifting athletes.
primary_outcomes: Lumbar Joint Position Sense-Flexion Repositioning Error
Lumbar Joint Position Sense-Extension Repositioning Error
Shoulder Joint Position Sense-Abduction Repositioning Error
title: Posture, Proprioception, Core Stability, and Balance in Weightlifters

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate whether watching a short humor-based video before surgery can reduce anxiety and negative emotions and increase positive emotions in patients undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy (gallbladder removal surgery). The study will also examine whether this intervention affects patients' quality of recovery after surgery.

Patients scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy will be randomly assigned to either a humor-based video intervention group or a control group. In addition to routine preoperative care and education, patients in the intervention group will watch an approximately 20-minute humor-based video before surgery. Patients in the control group will receive routine preoperative care and education without the humor-based video.

Anxiety, positive and negative emotions, and postoperative quality of recovery will be assessed using standardized questionnaires. The study will compare these outcomes between the two groups to determine whether the humor-based video provides beneficial effects during the perioperative period.
title: Humor-Based Video Intervention on Preoperative Anxiety Veya Humor Video and Recovery in Cholecystectomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to understand the influence of vaccine message medium (e.g., text, photo, or video) on intentions to vaccinate in college students.

The main question it aims to answer is:

* Does vaccine message medium influence intentions to vaccinate? Participants will be shown, at random, a photo, video, or text vaccine message and be asked to evaluate their intentions to receive the COVID-19 vaccine in an online survey.
title: Influence of Vaccine Message Medium on Intentions to Vaccinate in College Students

brief_summary:
Introduction:

Optimizing pain management after gender-affirming mastectomy (removal of breast tissue, aka top surgery) surgery is important for recovery and minimizing opioid use. While paravertebral nerve blocks (numbing the chest wall through injections near the spine) and injection of local anesthetic ("skin freezing") are two commonly used methods, it's not clear which of these techniques is best among patients seeking gender-affirming care. Previous studies on nerve blocks in breast surgery have mostly concentrated on patients having breast cancer removed. Studies show that paravertebral blocks are superior to skin freezing in breast cancer surgery. However, it has not been established whether this reduces long-term pain and works similarly in gender-affirming top surgery. This study aims to compare the how well nerve blocks work comparing to skin freezing for pain and opioid use after surgery.

Research question:

Does the use of paravertebral nerve blocks, as compared to skin freezing (aka wide local infiltration), reduce need for opioid use within the first 24 hours following gender-affirming mastectomy?

Hypothesis:

The investigators hypothesize that paravertebral nerve blocks are superior to wide local infiltration in terms of reduced need for opioid consumption in the first 24 postoperative hours for gender-affirming mastectomy (GAM) patients.

Methodology:

This randomized control trial will include adult patients undergoing GAM. The patients will be randomly placed into the either the nerve block group or the skin freezing group. Patients who are in the skin freezing group will also be sent to the block room where they will receive ultrasound and pressure to mimic the feeling of receiving a block. Pain will be measured using the 0-10 Numeric Rating Scale, and opioid use will be recorded at 24-, 48-, and 72-hours post-op. Given that most patient leave hospital on the same day, participants will complete a pain journal at home and will be emailed an electronic survey to submit their results. Quality of recovery will be measured at 3 days after surgery. A follow-up survey at 3 months will assess longer term pain using the Brief Pain Inventory. Phone calls to complete the survey with a member of the research team can be done by request.
title: Gender Affirming Mastectomy Analgesia Rial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of collagen-based absorbable nasal packing (NasoAid®) after nasal surgery. The main question it aims to answer are:

* The hemostasis 2, 12, 24, 48 hours after nasal packing.
* The endoscopic nasal assessments scores.
* The remnant percentage of nasal packing material.
* Patient-reported Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores for general assessment.
* Patient-reported outcomes, including the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test-22 (SNOT-22), Nasal Obstruction Symptom Evaluation (NOSE), and Total Nasal Symptom Score (TNSS).
* The incidences of safety indicators.

Participants will be randomized into either experiment group or control group, receive nasal packing at Day0, and re-visited on week 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12 after nasal surgery.

Researchers will compare if NasoAid® is non-inferiority to NasoPore.
primary_outcomes: Hemostasis Rate at 24 Hours After Nasal Packing
title: Efficacy and Safety of NasoAid® After Nasal Surgery

brief_summary:
Broken bones (fractures) are a common problem in several serious health conditions, such as osteoporosis, kidney failure, and sickle cell disease. To better understand and treat these diseases, researchers need a reliable way to measure how much blood flows through our bones.

In animal studies, a special scan called PET (Positron Emission Tomography) has been used successfully to measure bone blood flow. This scan uses a safe, low dose of a radioactive substance called sodium fluoride, which helps show how blood moves through the bones. However, using this method in people has been difficult in the past because older PET scanners were not sensitive enough to give accurate results.

Recently, St Thomas' Hospital in London has received two new, state-of-the-art PET scanners. These scanners can take pictures of the whole body at once and are much more sensitive than older models. They can also take images of the heart during the scan, which is important because it allows researchers to measure how much of the radioactive tracer is being delivered to the bones through the bloodstream. This is a big improvement over older, more invasive methods that required taking many blood samples.

The main goal of this pilot study is to develop a better, more reliable way to measure bone blood flow in healthy volunteers using these new PET scanners. The researchers also want to check if measuring the tracer in the heart is as good as, or better than, the previous method of taking frequent blood samples.

To do this, the researchers will invite ten healthy volunteers-men and postmenopausal women over the age of 50-to take part in our study. Each volunteer will have a one-hour PET/CT scan, which takes images from the head down to the upper thighs after a small injection of the radioactive tracer. To compare the new method with the old one, the researchers will also take five small blood samples from the volunteer's arm at different times during the scan.

The research team hope that this study will lead to better ways of studying and treating bone diseases in the future, making the process easier and less invasive for patients.
interventions: 1-hour Total Body PET/CT scan using the tracer [18F]-sodium fluoride
primary_outcomes: To measure bone perfusion (K1) and bone plasma clearance (Ki) with [18F]-sodium fluoride TB-PET/CT at multiple sites across the whole skeleton in 10 healthy volunteers, both are measured in units of mL per min per mL.
title: Development of an Improved Method of Measuring Total Body Bone Perfusion Using Total-body PET/CT

brief_summary: Rationale/Gaps in Existing Knowledge: Therapy of Infection-associated Secondary Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) in adult lacks evidence from randomized trial guiding first-line immunomodulation and current therapeutic practice primarily extrapolated from decades old pediatric HLH protocols and retrospective studies. In presence of infection very expensive therapy with intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) is preferred over Dexamethasone, however the comparative efficacy of IVIG and Dexamethasone alone remains undefined, especially in resource-constraints settings. (ii) Novelty: This will be among the first randomized controlled trials in adults with infection-associated sHLH, directly comparing efficacy of IVIG with Dexamethasone. The study uniquely integrates clinical outcomes with economic feasibility in a low-middle income setting. (iii) Objectives: Primary objectives will be to compare the efficacy of intravenous (IV) Dexamethasone and IVIG in achieving clinical remission and recovery of HLH-associated cytokines (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α, IFN-γ, GM-CSF) and Ferritin level. Secondary objectives include assessment of hematologic recovery, adverse events, and short-term mortality. (iv)Method: In this Randomized controlled open-label, non-inferiority clinical trial participants with sHLH, will be allocated (1:1) to receive either short-course of IV Dexamethasone or IVIG along with infection-directed standard care and will be followed-up for 4 weeks to evaluate predefined clinical outcome and laboratory parameters. (v) Expected Outcome: The study aims to establish whether IV Dexamethasone is non-inferior to IVIG for achieving clinical remission, recovery of HLH-associated cytokines level and reduction of short-term mortality. Results are expected to reform evidence-based, cost-effective therapeutic strategies for infection-associated sHLH and improve access to care in resource-constraint healthcare systems.
lead_sponsor: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh
title: Efficacy of Short Course of Intravenous Dexamethasone and Intravenous Immunoglobulin Therapy in Infection-Related Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (isHLH)

brief_summary:
As Saudi Arabia undergoes a transformative shift in public health through Saudi Vision 2030, targeting an increase in weekly sports participation to 40%, the cardiovascular health of women engaging in regular physical activity has emerged as a critical and research priority. Despite the rapid expansion of female-only gyms and competitive sports, there remains a profound lack of regional, sex-specific echocardiographic normative data and subclinical screening evidence for the Saudi female population.

This study is a prospective, observational cross-sectional, community screening study using handheld Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) to characterize physiological cardiac remodeling in recreationally active Saudi women and identify subclinical structural heart disease.
primary_outcomes: Left Ventricular Posterior Wall Thickness at End-Diastole (LVPWd)
title: CArdiovascular Phenotyping in Recreationally Active Saudi Women

brief_summary: This proposal will test the hypothesis that AKG supplementation will improve NGVC responses and cognitive performance in older adults. We will also test the hypothesis that these effects are mediated by a decrease in age-related oxidative stress within NGVU cells.
primary_outcomes: Change in neurogliovascular coupling using functional near infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS)
Change in neurovascular coupling using electroencephalography (EEG)

brief_summary:
This is an observational study in children up to 16 years old who are suspected of having central precocious puberty or delayed puberty. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can the level of insulin-like peptide 3 (INSL3) predict if a child's puberty has truly started?
* Can this marker help reduce the need for more complex and invasive tests?

Participants will:

* Give one extra blood sample just before starting the standard gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test (during the baseline blood draw).
* Have this extra sample used to measure the INSL3 hormone.
* Complete the rest of the GnRH test as prescribed by their doctor.

Researchers will compare the INSL3 hormone levels in children who have a positive GnRH test to those who have a negative test. This will help researchers learn if INSL3 can be used as a new, simple tool to diagnose early or delayed puberty.
primary_outcomes: Baseline INSL3 Concentration as a Predictor of GnRH Test Outcome
title: INSL3 as a Biomarker of Pubertal Activation: Role in Evaluating Precocious and Delayed Puberty

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to clinically evaluate the performance of 3D-printed composites compared to direct conventional composite restorations in Class II cavities
title: Clinical Evaluation of 3D-Printed Versus Direct Composite Restorations in Class II Cavities

brief_summary:
Lumbar spinal stenosis is a condition in which narrowing of the spinal canal can cause pain, neurogenic claudication, reduced walking ability, and limitations in daily activities. This study evaluated whether a 12-week structured, individually adapted exercise and exercise-counselling program could improve symptoms and physical function in patients with lumbar spinal stenosis.

Participants were randomly assigned to either an exercise group or a control group. The exercise group took part in supervised exercise sessions twice weekly for 12 weeks. The program included individually adapted exercises, treadmill walking, a progressive walking program with daily recording of walking distance or step count, and exercises to be performed independently at home. The control group continued with their usual lifestyle during the same period.

Outcomes were assessed at baseline, after 8 weeks, and after 12 weeks. The main outcomes were disability related to lumbar spinal stenosis, assessed with the Oswestry Disability Index, and walking capacity, assessed with the 6-minute walk test. Additional outcomes included pain, trunk muscle endurance, flexibility, balance, lumbar spinal stenosis-related symptoms and physical function, and health-related quality of life.
interventions: Individualized Multimodal Exercise and Exercise-Counselling Program
title: EFFECTS OF EXERCISE AND EXERCISE COUNSELLING IN PATIENTS WITH LUMBAR SPINAL STENOSIS

brief_summary: Anorexia nervosa (AN), characterized by abnormally low weight, a significant fear of gaining weight, and impaired body perception, is a psychopathological disorder with a 1% prevalence. This disorder has particularly high relapse and mortality rates, highlighting the need for improved patient care. Indeed, patients are often hospitalized, which cuts them off from their environment and contributes to the high risk of post-hospitalization. It therefore seems essential to develop intervention tools that can be used in daily life, to continue treatment in a self-reliant way outside the hospital. Several factors contributing to the maintenance of AN were identified in the literature, including an attentional bias away from food cues. We can also mention a deficit of interoceptive awareness (i.e. low awareness of one's own bodily signals), as well as higher levels of anxiety than in the general population. Physiological dysfunction has also been observed, both at rest and when exposed to food stimuli. Acting on these aspects has led to clinical improvement in several disorders, including anxiety and alcohol use disorder. Given these elements, the investigators propose the implementation of attentional bias modification training in patients suffering from AN. Attentional bias modification training's first aim would be the reduction of food avoidance, while secondary hypotheses postulate that the intervention could have an effect on interoceptive abilities and physiological functioning. This intervention, which can be used by patients themselves, has also shown its effectiveness in reducing anxiety. A reduction in anorexic symptoms and prognosis improvement is expected.
title: Anorexia Nervosa, Evaluation and MOdification of Attention

brief_summary: This clinical study aims to evaluate the effects of using the cosmetic product TRIDERM D.S. Crema Normalizzante in children aged 0 to 3 years with neonatal hyperseborrhea ("cradle cap"), potentially associated with manifestations of mild-to-moderate seborrheic dermatitis. The study will assess whether use of the product is associated with an improvement in the clinical signs of the condition, particularly scaling and erythema, and will evaluate its cutaneous tolerability. Caregiver-perceived improvement, as well as additional dermatological, photographic, and instrumental assessments, will also be considered.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) Score
title: TRIDERM D.S. Crema Normalizzante for Neonatal Hyperseborrhea (Cradle Cap) and Associated Cutaneous Manifestations of Mild-to-Moderate Seborrheic Dermatitis in Children Aged 0 to 3 Years

brief_summary:
The overall goal of the project is to enhance the physical and emotional well-being of primary school-aged children by incorporating short exercises-practicable within the classroom setting right at their desks-into their daily routines, thereby supporting their body awareness, flexibility, postural control, focus, and stress-coping skills.

Furthermore, the project aims to instill a habit of morning exercise among school-aged children and to determine the impact of this habit on flexibility, body image, pain, general well-being, and school burnout.
title: Physical and Psychosocial Outcomes of 16-Week Classroom-Based Morning Exercise Program

brief_summary: This clinical trial studies the safety of a computed tomography (CT) scan, with or without a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan, in planning for high-dose-rate (HDR) prostate brachytherapy treatment in patients with prostate cancer. Brachytherapy is a type of radiation therapy in which radioactive implants, such as pellets, seeds, ribbons, wires, needles, balloons, or capsules, are placed in the body, directly into or near the tumor. The radiation is delivered through a flexible tube called a catheter or a larger device called an applicator. Treatment planning, or simulation, is a process used to plan radiation therapy so that the target area is precisely located and marked. A CT scan is a procedure that uses a computer linked to an x-ray machine to make a series of detailed pictures of areas inside the body. The pictures are taken from different angles and are used to create 3-dimensional views of tissues and organs. An MRI is a procedure in which radio waves and a powerful magnet linked to a computer are used to create detailed pictures of areas inside the body. The addition of MRI to CT for HDR prostate brachytherapy treatment planning may help patients have less urine leakage and less pain after treatment.
conditions: Stage I Prostate Cancer AJCC v8
Stage II Prostate Cancer AJCC v8
Stage III Prostate Cancer AJCC v8
primary_outcomes: Mean Expanded Prostate Cancer Index Composite-26 (EPIC-26) Urinary Incontinence domain score
title: A Randomized Pragmatic Study of CT- Versus MRI-Based Planning for High-Dose-Rate Prostate Brachytherapy for Prostate Cancer

conditions: Gaining Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength
lead_sponsor: IRCCS Sacro Cuore Don Calabria di Negrar
primary_outcomes: Neurological assessment of motor function and sensation
title: Efficacy of Robotic Upper Limb Rehabilitation Training in Patients With Tetraplegia
